Believing it to be a karmic capability to manifest God, even the serpent dance (sarppam thullal) that originated in ancient times has become impossible to discard from our hands today. After that, by worshipping various kalari deities and displaying ferocity in various forms of worship, it is said that one attains the manifested power. How will our children understand this tradition acquired through dance, special rituals, and karma? Furthermore, do we have the time to study what our mothers or fathers tell us, or by sifting through the rights and wrongs that have come into our Vedic system? Or if we study, can we grasp anything? Because all kinds of shortcomings had come upon us like this, it took a long time just to follow the Yugadharma. So, when this Yugadharma begins, it will be something else entirely. It is seen through calculations that Kali is the shortest of eras. It has four hundred and thirty-two thousand years. So, can we call upon God only after this Kali era ends? It is said that Kali will not affect us. How did Kali not affect us? It is not like that. Kali is indeed good for all of us. What has been told to us and what our ancestors have taught us to this day is that Kali means destruction, isn't it? If our children themselves act improperly, attributing it entirely to the faults of Kali and explaining our own faults and virtues is the extent of our knowledge to this day. How can we find fulfillment in this knowledge? How can we act by knowing at least the dharma meant for us? It is a karma that we cannot accomplish in any way. However, by bringing forth these great souls here and there, no matter how they come before you, you must at least respect that the people sent by God have come to do that. Otherwise, you won't be able to accept it. For example, we could not understand Sri Krishna, who was born such a wise person. It was covered up with stories, turned into the most corrupted stories, changed into stories and plays, and became Kathakali. How much can we achieve in the karma of showing and informing that depicting all the evils in the land is our current intelligence?

When examining each of these instances, we realize how long God has been working for us! However, we have completely failed to understand this. You may all ask: if God is everything as claimed, why can He not just change everything in a single stroke? That is incorrect. Consider the vast expanses of time, even the very calculation of a 'Kalpa' that you have heard of. It speaks of the history of a Kalpa—whether remaining inactive for that entire duration or functioning throughout it—that has encompassed countless 'Chaturyugas' or countless 'Manvantaras'. Can we proceed on the right path merely by studying all this? We cannot. What, then, should we do? If a prophet suited to the times, a preceptor (Acharya), or any such great soul (Mahatma) arrives, how will we recognize this person? We are utterly incapable of knowing. This is the same across everyone's history. Our shortest measure of time is this Chaturyuga. How so? Because Kali Yuga has only just begun. How can we, who cannot even fully comprehend a span of merely three epochs, grasp the extensive history of this Chaturyuga? Since we lack information regarding any of this, we have merely been reading the records written and preserved by whoever established the calculations, wherever they did so. How, then, could these historians formulate such an extensive historical account? They cannot. That is precisely why, no matter how clearly they stretch or condense the narrative, it remains a story that does not extend beyond ten thousand years. This is evident even if we examine the knowledge we currently possess. There is no need to look at anyone else's accounts. Since the birth of Sri Krishna up to the present day, the great souls who have incarnated have attempted to reform us by speaking in the simplest of terms, through their births and by causing births. Yet, no one understood this. Nor does anyone know who this is. Having reached that state, we have all fallen and decayed into a course of action where no one respects anything; we have drained its vital essence and instead gathered worthless refuse. Consequently, we have become thoroughly corrupted. How can we rectify this? It can only be achieved if a great soul instructs you. No ordinary individual is capable of imparting this. No one can correct you, except for that specific individual who has been granted the absolute authority for these times.
Guruvani
Birthday Commemorative Edition - 2006
The Path of Dharma Transcending the Stream of Thought

Today, if an incident occurs anywhere in our known world, alternative mediums have emerged to present it before us instantly as news. That is a process that has evolved up to television, taking the place of true knowledge. Thus, you see this before you today. We live in an era where we lack the means to think and comprehend what this is or why it occurs in this manner. It does not readily yield to such thought. If we enter the stream of thought, what can we achieve other than pondering over various histories? We can achieve nothing. Therefore, we possess a trajectory of Dharma that inquires whether there is anything beyond this stream of thought. However, no community or nation has been able to grasp it. The familiarity we have with it today is constructed by intertwining all issues in a manner that merely incites us to fight among ourselves. Today, we are actively choosing the very place where the fortress of destruction—built by playing and manipulating the state machinery—has grown the largest. Every one of us is like that. What can those historical scholars who make these choices convincingly teach us about our true reality? Let each of you reflect upon this. Hence, if we, who are born and raised on a wretched path that is incapable of making us think, incapable of independent thought, and incapable of absorbing us into any real knowledge, try to figure out what we should become, it will prove futile. There is no point in invoking rationalism or theories of liberation (Mukti) for this purpose. If one speaks of the theory of Mukti, it cannot simply be taught. It is Mukti itself that is arguing. How can that be done? One who is bound to Mukti will have no time to tell you. If you hold any such understanding, please state it. You are all educated individuals. I am asking the educated. I possess no formal education. Therefore, you have the right to speak. Please do so. Thus, in this condition, it is not something that can be attained through mere study. Regarding that, as I mentioned earlier, the first university originated in our land; we claimed everything in its name. Is this not how we are taught? Are we not studying a history that claims when its scraps of paper were gathered and set ablaze, it burned for three months? What, then, are educated people like you going to serve here? What will you place into the hands of these children? You cannot offer anything. No historian can. No historical scholar can. Where do we currently stand regarding the actions we must undertake? Reflect on that as well. If we proceed without understanding that, we have no authority to articulate any justice concerning ourselves, our nation, or any part of the world. Let it be an educated or an uneducated person. Can we work and accomplish this to witness it as a reality within our lifetime? Is it an individual matter? No. What is required now? You tell me. What is it that we, who are alive today, need? Is it sufficient to merely patch together the remaining fragments of those stories taught by our parents and pass them on to our children? If so, that is enough. In that case, since the parents have already spoken it, does anyone else have anything further to say? When parents speak, they can only address other worldly matters. This is not the responsibility of the parents. Realizing this one truth, parents should admit, "Children, this is not it; we do not know. At least practice this; practice the acknowledgement that we do not know. As for what is known, practice that." Thus, if each of us—having degenerated to the extent of lacking even the authority to say this—can attain Mukti by highlighting every culmination of this destructive course of fighting among ourselves, then proceed along that path. Take the easy route. If you can accomplish something in this manner, then do it. Otherwise, there is no use in corrupting yourselves by repeating this story. You possess an awareness of Dharma, prompting you to ask whether this can be accomplished or not, and how it might be undertaken. How will you grasp this Dharma? I can only suggest a minor task for this. When I say 'minor task', I mean an easy task. It is not actually a small endeavor. None of you should approach it under the illusion that it is a small task. We, who have not even had the opportunity to hear and understand it, possess no capacity to distinguish between good and bad, or small and great. We can only boast meaninglessly by uttering such hollow words. Therefore, relying on historical truth, this is entirely impossible for us.
Guruvani
Birthday Commemorative Edition - 2005
The Field of Action Imparting Ideals in Accordance with the Yugadharma

We have learned our contemporary history itself in such a way that we cannot understand it properly. Whether you want it or not, and if you do, what it should be—to practice at least the dharma you have heard about, you must have a realm of action that imparts the idea, mind, and intellect. You should not try to fulfill this through anything else. It is not possible. In your day-to-day life, for the rich man, it is the rich man's loss or the rich man's profit. For the one who works daily, it is about uprooting the working class. Other than this state of affairs, regarding you or us, what has this world imparted to us? What all has been built for us in the name of this caste, religion, and class? You will not think about this either. Then how are you going to think about these good things and tell your children? Or how are we going to mold our children to imbibe a good personality? When all this slipped from our hands, they took it away, and it became an art of argumentation brought back by a certain group. Now this is 'Philo-rubbish' (a play on the word Philosopher). It is not philosopher. It is 'Philo-rubbish'. How are you going to understand things through this philosopher? So, the part where you claim to have reformed it to this level has become this corrupted. Do you know why I can say this? I can say this because I am uneducated. If you are educated, you cannot speak such nonsense. This is 'nonsense', in a way, isn't it? What a deception it is on his part to say it is 'philo-rubbish' in front of you educated people? So what we need to understand is that we, who study this philosopher, did not see what our predecessors had done. We hold the rest of the history spoken by many great men who came to honor that course of action. But today, we are unable to comprehend any of this. That is why I said, if we wander behind those historians, we will get nothing. Through history, you will not get a single word about the path where your contemporary human beings acted and failed, or where our ancestors failed entirely. Then what should be done? People who are your contemporaries must see, know, speak, and practice this, and guide you onto that path. There is no other justification for this. If anyone claims there is, it is contrary to the truth. It will not happen. Because, all the knowledge we have discovered so far has been taught to us by the sorcerers among us, to fight and win against foreigners, or to hand it over to them, take money, and make a living for ourselves. Who else is there? In this history that has been cast so far away, what will you pass into the hands of your children who stand ready to ask, know, learn, and teach who each of us is? If they have the right to it, you must preserve it. It cannot be otherwise. So what you need to understand from this is this: Look at whether the great men born in the history after the beginning of this Kali Yuga experienced happiness or sorrow. Gandhiji is a great man who was born as a mere materialist. Gandhiji had no spiritualism. You should not assume otherwise. Why? The Congress people portray him here as a spiritualist, do they not?
Disciple: The demands are not gaining traction.

Guru: If it is not working out, why carry it around? If it has no value, can't it just be discarded? Now we can say that it is good. What would be said in those days? We have come a bit further along. Nothing of the sort has happened. We did not study that history either. We could not grasp the magnitude of that sacrifice. We could not walk in the path of dharma either. Nor did we attain the aspect of virtue. This is the truth. Other than that, there is no point in us studying a lot of these things and reciting them somewhere. That is not why I am asking you. The question is whether or not we have fallen into the miserable state of being unable to give contemporaneity to such self-sacrificing people who embraced that way of life, and cultivate it within ourselves.
Disciple: The spiritual aspect has not been imparted.

Guru: There is no spiritual aspect at all. Let that be. We say that Mahatmaji is a person with a spiritual side. Let that remain so. You do not need to take that up anymore. Why? Mahatmaji teaches that Rama Rajya should come, right? This era of Rama—Sanskrit primarily teaches that so many Ramas have come. Where do we stand in that action which teaches 'Ramo Ramah cha Kalki Janardana'? If that brings Rama Rajya, how will things work out? It will not. You haven't known this either. So you learn and teach through history that a Mahatmaji like this came for the Vaikom Satyagraha. This Vaikom Satyagraha itself is like this. It was not to enter the temple. It was to arrive by boat at the western entrance and walk around it. I think boats are still taken there even today. Isn't it? So there was no right to go and board that boat. One had to row through that water, come from both sides, and get off there. Because it is the temple entrance. This is the incident. What is the incident that you have heard, known, spoken about, and studied regarding this? If this is our contemporary history, what would the past history be like? So, having understood this, recognize the misfortune that we are unable to move forward despite studying this historical truth.

Someone created the Vamana avatar in order to impart goodness to our country. We have been taught that Vamana trampled down an individual who was ruling righteously. Why was he trampled down? The justification given is that he was an Asura. What was the reason this Asura was able to rule and govern so well? That question remains unasked. It is also unknown what exactly imparted this Asura nature. Caught in a web of such myths, what can we, being completely uninformed, ask and comprehend? First, you must understand this. We have not been able to grasp this contemporary history. For what purpose did they conduct all this? So, remaining ignorant of any such matters, how can we pluck out the misfortune and falsehood that have crept into the actions we have praised and glorified to this day? If our children were to stand straight and ask us directly, what answer would we give them? This is our greatest misfortune. Let that be. How should we view it then? For that, you must look at Sree Krishna as a historian or a Yogeeshwara. What is a Yogeeshwara? Do we not praise the author of the Gita, referred to as Yogeeshwara, with expressions like "How many Yogeeshwara Krishnas". Then, having failed to recognize this Yogeeshwara Krishna, the author of the Gita, when he came, what is the point in now proclaiming that he is a Yogeeshwara, he is this, or he is that? If I speak extensively to you, what will you say? You will argue that Krishna did not simply die like that. There is another explanation. What is it? He was consumed in the fire of Yoga (Yogagni). Is that not sufficient? We all attained salvation. It is justified in this manner. Every one of us is still harboring such corrupt karma, blabbering, and enjoying telling stories. The one thing we must do to change this condition is to study, teach, and understand Krishna. You cannot proceed without, in some manner, thinking, knowing, acting, or suffering regarding that man up to the karma of that sacrifice. If you wish to know about such a matter, you must possess the desire, determination, detachment (vairagyam), and love to understand the state of any karma that aligns with the truth. What is this detachment? It is the profound respect for love. That is detachment. One should not learn just to say, "He holds a grudge against me, hence he did that." One must become a detached seeker of love. There are certain elements within us that demonstrate how we can attain that state. Why do we study those aspects? How long will the karma we are going to undertake with this love endure, where will it lead, and how can we successfully execute it? We must be capable of learning at least one such karma. That is possible only through a renouncer (thyagi). What kind of renouncer should that be? It is for this reason that we must view Mahatmaji as a renouncer. He did not come preaching something entirely different. That man is a true renouncer. How were we able to comprehend the richness of sacrifice he demonstrated before us, enduring the kicks of soldiers without making a grand spectacle of it? How did we learn it? This is what we must understand. So, what were we able to learn from Mahatmaji's love? We failed to adopt that steadfastness in detachment. To demonstrate that this has become completely chaotic, what do the administrators of today, who grew up through that lineage, or those who rule, or those who invoke his name, show us today? They showcase Mahatmaji's sacrifice. How can we possibly adopt this sacrifice? It is entirely impossible. If anyone has demonstrated the true nature of sacrifice in our contemporary history, we have not been able to grasp it. Furthermore, if we study the history of exhausted and weary individuals who argued rationally or spoke of salvation, claiming all this is non-existent or false, how far will we progress? These are the two aspects we have retrieved today. Therefore, we cannot accomplish this. Do not speak of salvation, nor utter any form of nonsense. It will not work. We cannot become worthy of worship without at least understanding the dharma we must seek out in our lifetime, the sacrifice inherent in that karma, the hardship within that sacrifice, and how we must endure that hardship. This is history. The one who walks around today with a label hung in front of him, claiming to be the greatest renouncer, has achieved nothing in the position of that duty. What could possibly be achieved? We have failed to adopt anything demonstrated by our ancestors in all such respects. This is precisely what the Prophet's prayer in the graveyard during his final days signifies. True Muslims will not deny its existence. If such a person exists, they will not say it is otherwise. Consequently, whatever karmic paths we have utilized to study about renouncers have all become entirely corrupted. This state is far below our dignity. Today, after arriving at a point of singing, speaking, playing, and making us play, they have a song proclaiming that God is love. "Who knew the love of God, O mind."

Who truly knew? As this question continually intensified, what is the current state? Now it is all about foot-tapping, beating, and jumping around. Is this not how it escalated? If it is claimed that God will manifest from this, what are we supposed to do? Therefore, no evidence is required to prove that we are flawed in every conceivable way. We ourselves stand as the ultimate proof for all of this. I am sharing with you something from my understanding regarding what we must do if we desire a transformation from this state. It is my personal knowledge. I am uncertain how you will interpret it. What is understood is this. That is, within the karma that articulates Sree Krishna's sense of dharma, visibly manifest the dharma referred to as 'Pratyakshavaham Dharmam' (visibly manifest dharma). This is its true dharma. This does not refer to the 'visible' that we perceive today. What have we currently comprehended by the term 'visible' (Pratyaksham)? All these poets, or the scholars of today, term it 'Pratyakshavadam' (empiricism/positivism). Consequently, what do they call the rising of the sun? In contemporary literature, it is described as "bursting forth," is it not? A sun that bursts and falls in such a manner is what we have here. So, if these charlatans could successfully impose all this upon your ignorance, where do you currently stand? Where is it bursting and blossoming? It is not bursting or anything of the sort. If they teach you about a void space and a non-void space within a course of action revolving inside these nine planets, will you ever transition away from this? If there is anyone educated among you, please state. Tell me whether we need to transcend this dharma of the times or not. Reflect on this yourselves. There is a profound utility to this. You must understand this. What is it? It is Krishna's 'Pratyakshavaham Dharmam'. That is precisely why Krishna questions Arjuna, asking, why would you not kill them? It is nothing else. I am unable to fight them in this manner, nor am I capable of killing them. It is solely in that karma of killing that I harbor this hesitation.
No, you must take a comprehensive look. Do you believe what I am telling you?
Absolutely.
Then why do you not believe me, the words that I
speak?
It is regarding the matter of killing them.
Alright, sit down and reflect upon it carefully.

Then it is said that he sat in that chariot itself with his eyes closed. That is what the Gita itself says, when he closed his eyes, he saw that there is no sin in killing them. Is that how God appears? According to your logic, for God to appear like this... Are you not saying that one should not cause pain even to an ant? How could you, who are so thirsty for compassion, feel like killing this? I am asking the historians. How can you feel like killing? Haven't you said that not even an ant should be killed? Then haven't you seen Jain theoreticians walking around nowadays? With cloth tied over their mouths. Then how can one who says that even germs should not be killed live here? Then should God proclaim that you and I are great sinners? How many creatures are you chopping, boiling, and eating? If another group says, "We won't eat any of these creatures," and instead plants these seeds, lets them sprout, cuts and eats them, and thus repeatedly cuts and eats their leaves and stems, is that not loss of life? Then what is it that you are going to establish with this Advaita philosophy? What kind of decency is this? This will not work. Then one thing that Arjuna saw you should be convinced of; that would be for your own good. "Why don't you kill them? You do not kill anyone, nor do you cause anyone to be killed"—if this is to be said, from what perspective is it being said? That is him, the writing of that intellect is good. What is it? It is said that he fought after reverently folding his hands. Whatever it may be. Whether it is a lie or falsehood, right or wrong. Whatever it is, it is an evident reality for us. Why? He fought after bowing to Krishna. Having fought, it is being asked to Bhishma lying on this bed of arrows, who is it? The very advocate of karma who caused the killing has done it. What is being said? You could have departed before this. Then why did you lie like this? That is when it is said, let this go Krishna, this will go. When we look into the historical truth of Bhishma and Drona that led to this being said, we can see who they are. When looking into it like that, what is its history? Bhishma and Drona falling like that, what is the reason for falling like that, or why did Krishna himself stand in this course of karma as disciple and guru and cause them to be killed, why did he kill them? - You will get an opportunity to think about this. Having thought about this, in this human dharma, what transpired then, what has transpired today, and what happened before, of that history's evident reality called dharma, you must attain that part.
Guruvani
Birthday Commemorative Dedication Edition - 2006
The Grandeur of Time

We have within us a combination of many good and bad elements existing together. Having distinguished this good and bad, how should we take them forward? Do we not need to find such a path? Now, having seen many eminent personalities with me, I cannot help but say this. However, they have all taught me good things. But I could not gain anything from that. The reason for this inability to gain is that the destination they speak of and believe in is not the right one. This earth has a celestial calculation. Similarly, we also see these three spheres. There are stars much larger than these. Is there not a sky surrounding them? Which among these skies can we count? There is no point in any of us speaking about this. Then, what lies beyond this? Should we not know what this administrator is? The world does have an administrator, doesn't it? Should we not know where He resides? When we reach there, we are standing on this celestial calculation. The accumulated karma of a soul extends only up to that point. Everything known, seen, and heard extends only up to there. It should be viewed as such. Then how can this be corrected? Therefore, each of these calculations has a light. We should not proceed by saying that such a light does not exist. It does exist. But how is it connected? Unless we know in how many ways it reaches where, and how far this connected part extends, one can only go up to that point and halt. Now, because we have this connection, do we not understand? The two things we mentioned have happened. One is that the light vanished. The other is that the other person accomplished what he had to accomplish. What was accomplished? It means that everywhere, our goodness will be conditioned and destroyed. You were not summoned here to watch a dance performance. It is to tell you something. The entire universe is permeated by inherent tendencies (*vasana*). Do you agree? Can we do this only after seeing all the goals permeated by *vasanas* that are present in each of us? If it is said that God is different, he will not even be able to drink water. If you go to North India, this flowing water where people spit—I have not seen it, but those with me have gone and seen it—when it flows and reaches another place, they can scoop it up and use it. That is how our God is situated. Is it not? That is Muslim water, this is Hindu water. Then which water are you going to drink? So, what will you do in a place where there is no Muslim water? We have a truth that belongs to everyone like this. Doesn't it? Then, how far has the path of yoga reached for this truth? What does our thought say when we speak of yoga? Yoga is said to be his fortune.
Disciple: Does it not mean the yoga of past lives? So, it means merging this *Jivatma* (individual soul) with the *Paramatma* (Supreme Soul).

Guru: Yes, exactly that. In every sense, there is only that. If anyone says anything beyond that, it is incorrect. However, as long as the reality of what constitutes the soul of the Supreme is not made clear, one can only speak foolishness.
Disciple: We do not see anyone having merged into the *Paramatma* across past lives in any of our *Manvantaras* (epochs).

Guru: Therefore, we do not even know whether what is called a *Manvantara* exists or not. The term Manu refers to the karma performed by one born as a human. Which Manu is that? Thus, how many *Manvantaras* are there? Which *Chaturyuga* is that? In which *Chaturyuga* does our birth and death occur? We have not been directed along this path. What is the use of proceeding without understanding this much? We will merely spin around just as the earth rotates in its orbit. There is nothing else to it. What would have been the situation if someone had said a hundred years ago that the earth rotates? Such a time did exist. Similarly, it is said that Lord Rama lived seventeen lakh years ago. If we keep saying that Lord Rama just passed by yesterday, will the matter be resolved? Thus, this is a change spanning over so many years.

How can a person who believes in Narayana Guru carry forward the arguments of liberation (Mukti) and rationalism (Yukti)? It does not mean they have understood one by following the other. Each of us has proceeded like this. Is it right or wrong? Therefore, if we say that the karma accumulated across these *Manvantaras* does not exist, where will we go? It is impossible. Are we not taught the *Manusmriti*? What is the *Smriti* (memory) of this Manu? It is what has been realized through life. How many Manus experienced that realization? Should we not study such a thing? There is no point in my convincing you by stating things that do not exist. Therefore, if the *Manusmriti* speaks of fourteen Manus, which Manu is this? Which Yuga is it? What all is within that Yuga? How many prophets, preceptors, and apostles are there? By such a count, how many preceptors have been enumerated to date? This is not a fraud or a scam. This is a good thing. I am glad that you possess that intellect. But my happiness is not enough. That is why I am saying this. How should we count these preceptors now? We can take the count over a crore of years. Is it over? Is there any use for you in taking it that way? The fact you cannot know in this life is that if you count a crore of preceptors, it stands as a count of two thousand, three thousand, five thousand, ten thousand, up to a crore of preceptors. We cannot proceed there. I am only saying this if you agree. I have not said that this matter is not in the calculation. Should we not understand in which era and for how long we have been recorded by considering the account of a preceptor? That is what I am asking. Now, in the tradition of prophets, the latest to arrive was Muhammad. Thus, how many prophets has this Muhammad mentioned? What will you do with the historical truth that this changed from one to become many prophets? The matter will not move forward by saying it doesn't exist. One cannot proceed by telling everyone it doesn't exist. Therefore, among the many praises bestowed, when referring to the final Nabi, the final Christ, or the final Prophet, what have these prophets done? Should we not respect that? If not, then leave it. When we respect each of them and proceed, we see a helpless situation where we are unable to reach a conclusion. That is why I said this. They eventually came and established as a final decree that one should marry at least four times. Right? How would it be to get them married without understanding what these four are? We must ascend from this condition. I asked what the path for that is.
Disciple: It must be brought about step by step.

Guru: Yes. When brought step by step, wouldn't this cage of the living soul be lost? We should not proceed merely by stating the meaning of the word and the meaning of the celebration. Regarding us, who are we? We cannot agree if just anything is said. We can agree if theories are stated. That is not a problem. Similarly, one can assert each historical truth and justify it. Therefore, do not believe that the world has ended. That is how it goes. So, shouldn't the calculations of these *Manvantaras*, the calculations of these prophets, and the calculations of theorists align? Otherwise, one cannot simply proceed by accepting whatever someone says as true. They have made a mockery by merely talking about this Yoga itself. A Yogi should not be in a house where there is a mother. They have made us read and listen to many such absurdities that they have spoken and established. So, the mother is a woman, the sister is a woman, the wife is a woman. What is being said here is the course of karma that one passes through as a man and a woman. We cannot move forward by saying that none of this exists. People have completely overturned us. This is how I say it. Now, Alathur Brahmanandan has written about idol worship and various other things across these fourteen books. But for whom is this? Is it for himself and his disciples, or for the people of the world? If it goes on like this, it won't work. We should not deny any of it. It exists. If it goes like that, there will be a slight difference, like the one who holds onto a thick rope and the one who holds onto a straw. Even this straw is long, isn't it? He also held on tightly. Similarly, let us evaluate it. Let us not proceed by denying anything! If so, up to where have these prophets reached and stood? What is that?
Disciple: Weren't the prophets able to lead only up to a specific point?

Guru: Yes. So, we must first agree to that. That is what the Prophet said. It is not said that what none of them did was complete. It was complete as far as it was done. So, it stands where the fourfold structure and the four states were mentioned. That is, what we need to understand is that they made us perform Yoga, Karma, Jnana, and Bhakti, forgetting the appropriate times they should be practiced. We follow a Yuga as four periods, don't we? If not that, we should at least respect the *Chaturyuga*. Therefore, one should not think that the karma of the other Yuga can be practiced in this Yuga.
Disciple: So, perform the actions of the respective Yugas in those respective Yugas.

Guru: So, the author of the Gita himself is saying that. We must respect it. He is describing the events for those times. The situation was such that it extended into another era, and Sri Krishna could not escape. The temporal distinction they wrote and taught us is incorrect. It can be used in all times. The wise can use it. It is said for that era: "Preserve your body to overcome Kali." See how strictly it is said? Others will not say this. Ours are the souls and minds that have experienced and exhausted countless lives in those eras. The question is whether this aligns with this *vasana* (inherent tendency). One sits thinking that sorrow, joy, birth, and death exist only in one's own life. That death, birth, and sorrow do not exist anywhere else. Do not think like this. When I say this, you might not like me. Because I am a sannyasi.
Disciple: That is applicable to everyone.

Guru: If it exists, know what it is and engage in karma to remove it. How is our soul tied down? Thus, one must not proceed by saying that the course of karma tying down men and women in this karma does not exist. It does. With what should it be controlled?
Disciple: Through devotion (*Bhakti*).
Guru: Yes. It can only be controlled through devotion. What is devotion?
Disciple: The devotion we show towards a divine consciousness.
Guru: There are many like this. Now, our lineage of prophets.
Disciple: There is only consciousness.
Guru: The question is, with what did we measure that consciousness?
Disciple: According to what the Acharyas have said.

Guru: Wasn't I telling the story of what the Acharya said? Didn't I tell the story of Sri Rama descending into the river? Then who attained liberation? Will it work if one says the body is not needed? What nonsense! It is said that this Sri Shankara jumped into a gorge. Why did he jump?
Disciple: No one can say what it was for.

Guru: It cannot be completed by saying such things. It is that "matter does not know, and knowledge has no thought." One cannot know through thinking. It is beyond that; it is beyond comprehension. So, the question is, what is the point of telling us to know through thinking in a place where knowledge lacks thought? Matter does not know, knowledge has no thought, neither will it dictate nor tell. Then what to do? One cannot just leave without touching anything. One must touch before going. Shouldn't we realize that we have such a deficiency? Having understood it, shouldn't we also know how to resolve it? This is where *Bhaktyayukto*—whatever is the substance of your devotion, keep it in front. Act with *Bhaktyayukto yogabalena*. The author of the Gita himself is saying this. With that devotion, wherever it aligns, one should reach there. That is its meaning. It is not about elaborating heavily on the meaning. Its meaning is exactly what the author of the Gita stated. We did not see it that way. One must act through *Yogabalena*. The union (*yoga*) of the living soul is there; that is what is stated there. Just talking and preaching won't work. What I am speaking is not a learned language.
Guruvani
Birthday Dedication Edition - 2006
How India's Error Came About (In the Order of Worship)

Shaiva, Shakta, and Vaishnava are all essentially the same. Based on the changing states, one group gives priority to Shakti; another group disagrees and gives it to Shaiva. Another group gives it to Vaishnava. This is the only difference. What they are saying is stating such differences. But that is not the real difference. One reaches a certain level only if one grasps the essence of this Shakta, Shaiva, and Vaishnava. Otherwise, both of these will remain there. All three must go together. If not, when you get there, they have established various stories to justify it. Shiva gave a boon to Bhasmasura. There is a story that when the boon was given, he went to touch Shiva's own head. Like this, they sent it to three places, and after running to three places, nobody could achieve it, and he was told to go to the one who gave the boon. Similarly, when you reach there, such an error will occur. One must proceed by fulfilling all three. If one holds onto one, one must attain that Vaishnava, Shakta, and Shaiva. Proceeding without doing so is the greatest disaster for India.

It is said that there are many gotras like Parasurama Gotra, Viswamitra Gotra, and Sri Sankara Gotra. All these are contained within this Trimurti. When speaking of this purity of gotra, these four must be included—Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaisya, and Sudra. If it does not accommodate all four of them equally, when this purity of gotra is considered, they will drift apart. That is the mistake that has happened in India. When we get a vision in this manner—now, when a Vaishnava's turn comes—they will explain the matters of Vaishnavas to them. When a Sakteya's turn comes, it cannot be explained why it happened so to the Sakteya. There is a Sakteya lineage, isn't there? Now ٹ Shakti lineage or Shiva lineage. If this comes, this Guru cannot explain this. That is the problem in it. This is what has happened to India to date. The Vaishnava will say he is great, the Saiva will say he is great, and the Sakteya will say he is great.
Disciple: I have a doubt. It is said that the Saiva will explain his matters. Then, can the others speak about the power of Shiva?
Guru: They cannot explain it. They haven't explained it reciprocally. They will say it is fine, it is good, upon seeing it. So, what did you understand?

Disciple: What the Guru is saying is that, if one proceeds with such a sense of difference, nothing else will be gained. It means they understood that, as the Guru says, one can achieve it only if one sees everything and goes through everything.

Guru: So, after that, when our Trimurti tradition was completed, the status of Devendra, the status of Parashakti, the status of the Ganas—the Guru is the one who has attained this. Otherwise, it is said that this cannot be attained.

So, because this was not explained in this way, we do not know about the Manvantara. Since this is a flawed aspect, in our India itself, they separated into three and began fighting among themselves. When that happened, we could not stand united. Therefore, over a long period, our Asian continent separated into many pieces due to natural disasters. How many countries are there in Asia? When we speak collectively now, which ones are called Asian countries?
Disciple: Pakistan, China, India, Russia, Japan ٹ

Guru: So, the reason these continents drifted apart like this is because they stood apart and acted like this. Every time the yugas change, there will be some calamity. Now, as an example for that, Jupiter is a huge planet. They say that a comet recently crashed into Jupiter and its face changed. In the future, when we look at it, it will be a place lying in ruins. That much area collapsed and broke apart.
Disciple: There is such a place in Mexico. There is a crater there with a diameter of 180 kilometers. It was struck like this two crore years ago; just like it struck Jupiter.

Guru: So, to comprehend such profound depth, we must know this Manvantara. The Gurus did not go that way after understanding the Manvantara. When the Asian countries lay together, some people had entered here. They also lived according to the customs here. As it broke away like this, they separated into individual countries. A few remained here. They used their intellect to learn these mantras and tantras and created the Vedic religion here. Thus, the Vedic scholar is the authority here. That is the problem here. That is also the reason why people do not unite. Similar things exist there too. But what is there is not this powerful. It is a different method. We will not touch and take this, we will not touch and drink—in such a way, standing far apart, we humans became distanced from each other. Clinging to these mantras and tantras, they went after gods and goddesses. So, when they went like that in this Trimurti system, this karma associated with the four-faced one (Nanmukhan) became non-existent. Nanmukhan—that is, the one who created the four Vedas. That is Nanmukhan, Brahma. No other histories about that Brahma emerged. If the history about Brahma is to emerge, the Manvantara must come. So, when the Manvantara was lost, the history about Brahma was also lost. That is, Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesa are what we call the Trimurti. Brahma is not that. If we say Brahma, assigning a specialty (other than Brahma-shakti), then when it comes, the Manvantara will come. So, when the Manvantara was not studied, knowledge about this Brahma was lost. We only know that Brahma exists. How this is, was also not clearly understood. So, in this Trimurti, in the place called Brahma, they imagined Brahman and moved on. Brahman means that which is contained in everything. Brahma is not that. It is the creative karma. We ended up believing in this concept of Brahman that it is paramount. It is not like that. So, if we want to tell the story of Brahma, we need this Manu. History says that such and such a person, the son of Surya, gave it to Ikshvaku. So, that history then does not speak of the Manvantara. When that happened, we went wrong. Having proclaimed the determination of Brahman, the Vedic system arrived, dividing and dividing into the four gotras of Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaisya, and Sudra. Thus, everyone claimed that what they held was the greatest.
Guruvani

The Truth to be Cultivated in the World

What is meant by *Pratyakshavaham Dharmam* is the fortune to see the various realms where the souls of our ancestors remain stranded. It is this fortune that our children should attain. There is no use in merely stating justifications. Thus, one must hold firmly to the truths that Sri Krishna realized and imparted. Krishna himself has shown a reason for you to reiterate that holding on so firmly is dangerous. That is, at the very end, when he fell down, the hunter wept, and Krishna, declaring that there was no saving him, asked to at least take away and save the women and children. Having heard, known, and learned all these words, why do you begin like this again? So, to praise whom are you doing this? Therefore, you cannot proceed in this manner. What should be done then? We need a direct perception (*pratyaksham*) of it. First, that must be attained within the waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states. Do not merely narrate tales. Thus, in your lifetime, most of you will not be able to witness this. However, a few among you have come as qualified individuals. Why is that? If it remains in your experience during the waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states, there are certain individuals you will perceive during those times.

Therefore, what is being taught to us is who Krishna is and what Krishna did. Similarly, we are being taught about the Trimurtis, which speak of the antecedent state. Thus, when it is said that the entity who plucked off Brahma's head is present here, what does that action compel us to think? Who plucked off Brahma's head? Why does this Subramanya worship the one who plucked off the head of his guru and god? Consequently, this four-faced deity—whose head was plucked off along with the heads of fathers, mothers, gurus, and ancestors—now has only three faces. It is said that the other head was plucked off. Now, if each of you were to get angry, how many of your fathers' and mothers' heads would be lost? There are people here who have concocted and served such stories. This is not what I have told you. Thus, you can perceive it in this manner. *Pratyakshavaham Dharmam* means witnessing it manifested right before us. It involves elevating and demonstrating what Krishna is, what a Guru is, what God is, what Shiva is, and what Brahma is. This is *Pratyakshavaha Dharmam*. It is not merely claiming, "I saw Jesus," "I saw Krishna," "I saw them," or "I saw these people." Rather, it must lead to a path of action that demonstrates what Subramanya, the one who plucked the head, and the one who did not pluck the head, do together. This is the true vision. We are not speaking of an action that is merely settled through pretentious talk and judged by karma. We must not practice such a dharma. God has given us a profound opportunity to fully accomplish this. This is what I am telling you. Therefore, it is said that we can attain knowledge in this state. How can one attain knowledge in this state?

Many great souls among our aforementioned ancestors, who have known and spoken the truth, must come before us. Upon their arrival, they must explain the historical truth of this matter. You must ask the Guru whether it is true. Only thus can this be known. If you wish to know it in that manner, can you go into asceticism (*sannyasa*) now? In this state, there is a duty you can demonstrate to your children. Both men and women. Having discovered this, you must find out whether there are countless such children in our country, or if we are being fed lies. To know this, you tell grand tales, do you not? How so? 'Gold must be tested on a touchstone.' What does that mean? The grinding stone is just lying there, isn't it? Can't we just grind it on that? Then why search for a touchstone? Therefore, it will only be correct if we rub it on the kind of stone where its purity can be ascertained. Otherwise, one will just keep grinding it on the regular grinding stone forever, without ever knowing its true value. This is what you need to understand. I am saying this after seeing both men and women; this is not a task done for a single caste, a single religion, a single region, or a single country. Therefore, you must learn it through such individuals. After knowing it, you must desire to serve it through your own efforts and your own love. This is what I have to tell you. I handled it this way to avoid speaking at excessive length about this. Both men and women must be able to boldly state that this is the truth. No other justifications should be offered. Statements like, 'She is a woman, she won't attain it; he is a man, he won't attain it; he is a scoundrel, therefore he has no God,' cannot be accepted here. If the scoundrel, the drummer, the mahout, and the farmer are all children of God, they must attain it. So, if they are to be children of God, they must reflect on what that entails. That is its true aspect. I did not do this to tell you, 'You will not get it, but you will get it if you just jump around.' It should be viewed in this manner: *Jagrat* (waking), *Swapna* (dreaming), and *Sushupti* (deep sleep). First, let you perceive it this way. You must not deviate from history or abandon the truth. Then, just as you perceive in the waking state, you must perceive in the dream and deep sleep states, and similarly in *Turiya* (the fourth state of consciousness); only after seeing it there should you undertake the journey towards *Turiyatita* (the state beyond the fourth). You have been blessed with the fortune to come to that duty. You must reflect on what you need to do to reclaim this fortune. By thinking, knowing, and acting upon this, even if we lose everything, what can we do with the consciousness of truth? That is your resolve, that is your duty, that is the truth you uphold. It is to prepare you for this truth that I speak. If Jesus could be beaten like this, people will come to beat and kill you too. No one who runs away saying 'I don't want to die' needs to come. At least if you are terrified like that, you won't come, right? So, all those who were searching for this were subtly tricked. But we have unraveled this trick. You must understand this. Therefore, you must attain the subtle body of these past ancestors. In which realm of the atmosphere does this subtle body exist, and from which realm does it control you? What is the structure of that realm, what all happens there, and how can you be guided into the narrative of what occurs there? Your Guru is the one who explains this to you. Seek and find it, and inquire wherever you need to inquire. Similarly, may this knowledge come to your children, and may those children become everything for the country. It should not remain confined to your home. That is not good. If it stays confined to your home, when you finish consuming all that you have amassed, he will die, you will die, and I will die. Right? Therefore, we must move completely towards a dimension of knowledge. This is your fundamental need today. I have stated that there is no harm even if your properties, house, or other belongings are sold to fulfill this need. Why is that? It is the very same word spoken by Jesus: that a wealthy man cannot easily pass through this path. Does that mean throw away all your money? It doesn't just mean that it is a word spoken by Jesus. If you hold onto the arrogance of wealth, we will not be able to progress. You do need money. I didn't say you don't need money. You don't need to argue that there is no God just because someone wrote a story elaborating on it and left. It doesn't mean that this applies to the rich, the beggar, and all the great sinners who are labeled as poor. The one called poor has merely swallowed his condition of poverty. What will he do now? This is the state of the 'poor.' So, if you set out to reform all these poor people in the land, the matter won't succeed. Therefore, do not prepare to dress up these poor people in this manner and invite criticism! Do not proceed to that destructive act of creating a situation where these poor people become even greater sinners and are forced to stretch out their hands before you, thereby destroying them. They are being driven to the brink of destruction. This is not how you uplift the impoverished. First, let him acquire the knowledge to earn and sustain himself. What is it? How does one earn and eat? People should offer it when they see you. That is what is meant by earning and eating. Let's do one thing. Let's make a man walk through here without a single thread of clothing. What happens? Will he get clothes? Similarly, if I sit down to eat saying I am hungry and go around barging in everywhere, won't they give us food? So, none of that is sufficient. Upon seeing you, clothing, wealth, capability, love, respect, and humility must all emanate through you; this must reach the country, and the children meant to implement this *dharma* must be creatively entrusted into your hands.
Guruvani
Birthday Revered Dedication Edition - 2006
Introduction to the Ashram and its Administration

There is a certain conceptual knowledge we have held onto regarding the antiquity of the ashram. We do not know how that understanding of the ashram came to us. When we hear the word 'ashram', we solely assume it to be a place designated for asceticism (*sannyasa*). That is not the case. However, because we do not think in that direction, there is another complication as well. History states that children were taken to Kanva, Sandipani, and others to study there. For what purpose? Were they taken there to become ascetics? It is recorded that even Sri Krishna lived in the ashram of Sage Sandipani. For what purpose? Was he taken there to become an ascetic? There are even those among you who believe that one must not go to an ashram. And furthermore, women are strictly not allowed to enter an ashram. This is a certain perception you hold. Why did this ignorance take root in you? You do not reflect upon that. You failed to understand that this is merely the remnant of a historical practice that traditionally forbade you from possessing education, wealth, and authority—even forbidding you from wearing proper clothes or learning the alphabet. Consequently, what happened? Those who taught history taught it in this distorted manner. They taught that a *sannyasi* is someone who sits silently somewhere, doesn't even require food, or if they consume anything at all, it's merely raw water or a leaf. You acquired knowledge in this flawed state. Is there any historical truth in this? You haven't even investigated whether there is any validity to it or not. You lack the foundational knowledge to investigate in that direction. Because of this lack of knowledge, what have you become? Today's Brahmin is the one who possesses any knowledge about it. Even among them, it has not been properly investigated why one goes to an ashram like this. Thus, both the Brahmin and the Chandala end up standing in the exact same state of ignorance. What is to be done?

It is said that for this system to be good, there must be the blessing of a Sadhu (sage). What is this Sadhu? You don't know that either. So, it is to improve the system and to learn about life that one is placed in this ashram. Not that it became a place for asceticism and the children were just dumped there--the ignorant injustice of saying such things still resides within you. What to do? What happened to you because of that? Whatever is done for you, you have no realization. You are unable to regain that knowledge. You, who have spoken and learned here so many times, were told a word that those who perform Gurupooja here must be careful. That is not just a single word. It was an obligation meant to be maintained until the end. But because you don't know this, you do not have the heartfelt determination to respect and understand it. What is the reason for that? You have been taught that after existing as this god and goddess, all souls are sitting under this god. What is the point of sitting under that god? You don't know that either. The reason is that none of you have paid attention to the knowledge called Manvantara. You don't know how long a Manvantara is, or how many Chaturyugas make up a Manvantara. So, we have swallowed a lot of such ignorance together. We cannot do anything about this. No matter how much is told to you, it doesn't enter your head. I see five or six new faces among you. I am not talking to them. Let them just listen. You who are called the old-timers don't pay attention to this at all. That is indeed a matter of great pain and sorrow. What is told to you as soon as you come? There is a karmic residue behind us, worshipped and made to be worshipped by our ancestors. It is coming and attacking us. We are the remnants of a corrupted karmic residue that manifests as disease, poverty, demonic children, various violent tendencies, and those who never fit in with the family. It would be a wonder only if we didn't have all this. How should we obey this? How to adapt to it? All this was explained to you before the Gurupooja was done. Or else, you don't have to do it. There are people here for two to four years who still haven't done Gurupooja. They are not allowed to do Gurupooja. What do you think that means? Let someone older here speak.
Disciple: Does it mean it should be done only after gaining that maturity?

Guru: You are not able to. For how long have I been teaching this. We have realized that the flaw of what was done is within us. Then why can't it be done? We say in a word that it is due to the lack of the meritorious aspect (punya) of the soul. That is true. But, are you gathering the strength to assume that you don't need this merit anymore? How will you understand that? The meritorious aspect is needed. How is that? Should God give the merit?
Disciple: It is the fruit of karma that is being experienced.

Guru: Then, where will the children born again be, when your karma is standing flawed like this? If you do not behave carefully regarding this, no one can do anything. I did many things and explained many things properly. But if only this matter is told to them, they will not obey. Because you do not act with knowledge, how many mistakes have occurred because when a karma is done and things get straightened out, you don't obey and the family doesn't maintain it? There are countless. There are so many people in here now! Should I do this and be ruined like this, or is it enough if you ruin yourselves, or should everyone be ruined together? You must give an answer to that.
Disciple: No one should be ruined.

Guru: Indeed. But, what is it like? Can it be achieved through your unnecessary actions? Your children are not the ones to understand that we have a medium to know things in advance and that what we accomplish is a special ordinance of upholding dharma and karma through that medium. Your children were not born in that way. What is it? You are the type of people who offer vows and offerings to God to get things done. How lowly you are, trying to win God over by giving offerings. Why are you keeping quiet? I am asking, what is the special virtue residing inside that intellect which thinks it can gain things by giving vows and offerings to God?
Disciple: Isn't that how parents have taught us?

Guru: Yes, they taught you. If you somehow come to know what is needed to change from that, don't you need the honesty to accept it along with your home, your land, and your country? Are you showing the harmonious nature to act in accordance with that? Do you show it in your home or outside?
Disciple: We don't have the capability.

Guru: It is because you don't have the capability that I am asking this exactly like this. It is because I understood you lack the capability. Shouldn't we at least be able to understand that each of us is the owner of a mind that cannot be reached even if we try? This is what is impossible. You cannot. If there is any opportunity, you interject your intellect, insert something else into it, and from within it, you hold on to every embodiment of ignorance that revels there. Nothing can be done. You do not even desire a truthful life. What to do? Even if you have the desire, it is like this. You cannot do it. You don't know what it is. This itself is our flaw. Has this happened to one family, one caste, or one religion, or is it present in all human beings? Is this present only in our India right now? Do you believe that this exists and is taking effect in us?
Disciple: Yes.

Guru: It is not enough if only one person speaks. If any of you have any theories of rationalism or liberation, you should state them. After demonstrating liberation-theories, rationalism, and nonsense, and then when paralysis strikes, you just surrender to it. Is it not so? What have you assumed? In the realm of knowledge, you are getting nowhere. Whatever has come down to you from the state, all of that is a course of action that ruins you and this world. What is the state like in that regard? The state is an ignorance that twists the perspective of the nation for the sake of caste, for religion, and for temporary needs, only to stab the people in the back. Apart from further increasing this ignorance time and again, are you capable of doing anything else? You are all smart. If asked why you are smart, you would not know. To you, this seems like a new matter, and you keep shifting aimlessly without reaching anywhere. How are the greatest writers? How are the greatest thinkers? In all such ways. Likewise, whoever it is, every tramp out there has ended up like this. What do you have to say in response to this? Are not each of you the ignorance taught by a doctrine that has forgotten to be humble or to show respect with love? Or are we all standing apart from all that? So, each one of us is eagerly taking up the culmination of the lowest kind of life that has crept in through ignorance, lack of experience, and habit. None of you wants to improve. Or is it that you act with the assumption, "Let illness come to me, no matter what happens, I will only do this"? If anyone has anything to say about that, let them speak. As far as we are concerned, for every thinking creature, or anyone wishing to grow—not just humans, but for all—this is a great destruction scattered like a storm. What do you feel like saying? You speak. I have asked you in various ways many times. But you will not say it. Either keeping quiet like those who know, or keeping quiet like those who do not know, or engaging in karma that perishes after attaining intellect—I cannot understand what it is. If elderly people like that mother ask this, I do not answer. Why? Because if told, they have reached an age where they can neither grasp it, follow it, nor impart it. What do these elderly mothers tell us? "We have done everything we had to do. Now do as you please. If necessary, I will just walk out." Where to? To take up asceticism (*Sanyasa*). Then do one thing. Just let all the elderly people go. Let them go away from our houses. At least they will not trouble the house, right? They will go their own way. Then they are going to sing that they have nothing. How much ignorance is assumed when saying this. It is the ignorance that comes when asceticism and family life (*Grihasthashrama*) mature. There are our ancestors who matured in asceticism. What is to be done? So, what we have assumed is that asceticism is a weapon to be taken up when all strength is gone and the nerves refuse to straighten. How did such lowly desires come among us? That is it; if it is known that someone went to an ashram, it is a quarrel. What did you understand? Did you not understand that it is the remnant of bad progeny? Did you not realize that these children are the amassed personification of ignorance, unable to distinguish what an ashram is, what a *grihasthashrama* is, what a *brahmachari* is, what a *karmi* is, or what a *jnani* is? We are the mothers belonging to this category. Right? What can be gained from this mother? Even then, the stubbornness remains the same. Which is? Let people hear the mother say that the children are the ones who do not give her water. One meaning is like that. Another meaning is, "Just like so-and-so's mother and father walked out, I will also go away, listen." That is another remnant of this. So, look at how the knowledge formed by the culmination of ignorance in this state resides in us. And then, after hiding under some flag or banana tree or in the paddy for a few days without being caught by the police, escaping from their hands, polishing himself up and wearing a shirt, parading as a leader, and bringing the third generation coming after him into this nonsense—such are the parents of today. When I speak the truth of this, you should be able to say it as it is. Speak. It seems no one here has brought their tongue. Having lived and learned so badly like compasses pointing north and compasses pointing west just to raise these children so wretchedly, who can reform you? I can say whatever I want. That is why I am scrubbing and washing you like this. I am peeling you. Even so, if I see that your mind grasps it somewhere, that is good. Speak, they sit here without a tongue, nose, or head. For our mother and father to be in this state, we must understand what their ancestors had made them believe. Having raised them and transferred the incompetence of merely pampering the children, they have become mothers and fathers. Is it true? Even after aging like this skin, to protect these children, they possess an ignorance that overrides their intellect.
Guruvani
Birthday Commemorative Edition - 2006
What can be earned behind the interpretation of letters

There is a karma I have been performing for so long. The pain is that not even a handful of households have realized and adopted this. It is not due to a lack of experience. Let them say that they are not obeying it because of a lack of experience. They are people without inclination or innate nature. This is the reason. You cannot buy this from a market. You can only handle this if you have the sense of dharma to imbibe it through your life. Otherwise, there is no point in you doing this. You will not gain anything either. I am saying this out of sorrow. What can be said to you who, despite so many people understanding it, have sought such an unfortunate acquaintance that you cannot even make your own household understand? In your home, where you speak of your wife, children, mother, and father, you live bearing the misfortune of being unable to impart it to them. What can be done about you who have become the biggest demanders to impart to others, reveal it, and dance like oracles again? Tell me what to do. Having understood this, you should do something; children, there is a karma that is shared with our lives—have this father, mother, or others been able to tell you what to do for it? I said, in the karma achieved over these twenty-nine years, I have done this for thousands of households. What is the significance? Even among the households that received it, there are many present here now. If anyone among them wants to say it is not so, let them say it. What can be done if one is born into such an unfortunate acquaintance? This is the pain. And yet, acting smart, they are all trying to climb up by pulling everyone else down. What is it? Lack of purity of intention. Possessing the greatest baseness. Children who never hesitate to behave unjustly at all times. Those who never undertake dharma. Isn't this the essence of what you show? So, I have failed after telling you this many times. There are also those in this crowd who come without knowing me. But those of you who have become acquainted have made me such that I cannot even say a good word to them. This is my asset. What can I do with you? Therefore, those of you who are incapable of understanding this and doing it yourselves should not go and ruin yourselves like this, nor should you come in this manner. If you desire any goodness in this world, it cannot be achieved except through love. If you believe this, you should not think that you can manage it with your prestige, foolishness, and militant strictness. Everything will catch fire! You will understand that. Why do you lead a life that you can never undertake? Where are you looking as you live? It is becoming agonizingly painful. Ask yourselves sincerely, what are we doing? This is a matter from my experience. Now, for those of you who come here—this is being said for those who do not know. What I am saying is nothing like the ashram sanyasa or matters you have heard of until now. You are seeking the greatness of the scholarship of one who is ruined without merit from an unfortunate karma, pretending to be a distinguished scholar despite lacking knowledge. This is your measuring rod. Where will you keep it to measure? So much buffoonery rests in the hands of the scholar. What is he showing off? Giving meaning to every letter, vowel, and consonant, interpreting it, using the sphere of influence of the letters reversed through vowels and consonants, interpreting the letter, and as if bringing you self-experience through that, what can you earn behind this interpretation of letters? Isn't that foolishness devoid of experience? Therefore, it does not mean that one should not study or teach this. Let them teach. You should also teach by explaining this. If not studied, one cannot know what these things are; having known, each of these practitioners trains to hide within us the most harmful karma that is entirely untrue and subjects us to contrary thinking. They are never those who have earned merit. This is why the nature of an avatar and the nature of God are spoken of and linked together. If someone grows up, they will make him an avatar. This is an imposition of the Hindu religion. Otherwise, a male saint or a female saint—what do they have in their hands other than building a fortress of destruction by saying something? What are they daily imparting to these children? Therefore, you must think thoroughly: what should be done?

I am saying this, an ashram is not for sanyasa. An ashram is not at all necessary for sanyasa. Then, it is needed. For what? When he embraces sanyasa and feels that life is completely fulfilled—he has truly renounced, and I am not talking about the matter of simply wandering somewhere — for him, an ashram and its support are needed. Likewise, I told you earlier that a place without sadhus is inherently corrupt. Who are these sadhus? They are these aforementioned sanyasis. They are the virtuous ones. You will not find anything worldly in them. They are not those who lived with ulterior motives. Whatever you do for them is never too much. But this money, intellect, and education used to feed, fatten, and destroy people is not the karma of sanyasa. Sanyasa is not of that nature. What is it? It means being completely blessed. That is what you must understand. Education, wealth, and sovereignty will all reach the place where he resides. This is sanyasa. It is not about saying he doesn't want any of this. All this is required. How will you protect it? This is what you must preserve. With what will you protect it? To protect your wife, children, wealth, sovereignty, and education, what will you use as a shield? I do not know why you begin to take upon yourselves the negative karma of this ignorant —this arrogant action. Please, those who are unfamiliar with me, at least keep these words in mind. Those who know me are the ones who fail to accept them. Let them be. Therefore, having understood this, you must also comprehend why you have undertaken the karma associated with worldly life. Otherwise, there is no point in wandering here and there wasting your time. What is the reason for stating this? That sense of defeat which your and my ancestors harbored as they grew up cannot simply be discarded anywhere. We are accepting this, taking up the karma and dharma, in order to contribute children who are rightful heirs to virtue. This is only possible through your life. It cannot manifest through a sanyasi. So, this is the karmi. You who accept that karma neither follow dharma nor acquire virtue, but walk around creating chaos in sheer obstinacy. Ignorant writers impose upon your heads intellect, and with withered minds and knowledge, you wager and perish, firmly binding yourselves to the path of karma. Think about whether this is true or not. But I absolutely must tell you this. I can. I am saying this because I see it. If you ask why I said it that way, I can give you an answer. Should you really make these children travel on such a disastrous path? You think about it. Each of you is a householder. You are not householders, not citizens, you are not even fit to be isolated individuals. You are ruined. I am forced to say this. What are these kids exhibiting before me even after I have done so much for them! Who might these children be who are trying to entrust me with this karma? What are they intending to do to me? They have not only completely destroyed their diligence, they are prepared to destroy even their lineage. It is painful to see this. If they can claim otherwise, let them say it and prove it. You have understood this much. Understanding this is sufficient. Going forward, I will only speak in this manner. Embracing the absurdities of entirely unnecessary systems, each one of you has turned into the offspring of children who have never been touched by a sense of dharma and have lost all humility. Have you considered what to do about this? Now, I will only say this. Because, I have affectionately told you multiple times. It won't work. You are not willing to take it, nor to give it, nor to receive it. Well, will you discard it? You won't do that either. You are merely existing in this state. So, what did I mean by saying this? You do not know what an ashram is. You do not know what grihasthashrama is. You do not know what a brahmachari is. You do not know what a sanyasi is. You do not know what a karmi is. Without knowing anything, you acquire everything—a shroud of ignorance. What can be done to this shroud? Even if you cleave it apart, it will not be destroyed. Even if you set it on fire, it will not be destroyed. So fiercely has it permeated the very essence of life, it is the culmination of ignorance. What are you going to do? Who can pardon this ignorance that stubbornly insists you will never accept this? Reflect on whether this is the outcome of my long-standing acquaintance that you have served me. Are you even human? After enduring so much pain, what reproach have I heard, what good have I heard—lacking even the wherewithal to inquire into this, you stand on the precipice of an immense ruin. It is not because you do not understand this. Having understood, it is the sheer arrogance of deciding 'let my understanding remain with me'. Because, once he understands this, does he not have to regulate his own household? To avoid regulating it, his path of karma is to let things unfold as they please. Having proceeded thus, the rest is left for the children. Can one degenerate to this level? Grihasthashrama is not meant for such degradation. Absolutely, if life, wealth, and prosperity are required, grihasthashrama is the karma capable of governing the very nations of the world. It is their children who come and display all this. So, is your notion merely to survive somehow, living according to my abilities, and when my time is over, let everything else sink into the Arabian Sea? Are you not displaying a ruined life? For whom are you exhibiting this? Agonized, unable to tell you the truth, I ended up trapped in a hapless acquaintance. What to do? Henceforth, I can only speak to you in this manner. I state this with profound sorrow. Do whatever you will. I do not know if those residing here even reflect on the path of karma demonstrated toward the men and women who come and go here. You are that depraved. Why do you even come? There is absolutely no purpose in your coming here. What do you come to attain? If you are capable of accomplishing it, then do so. Otherwise, you need not feign any decency here, nor display any lack thereof. I am that repulsed. I am speaking the blunt truth. What is it? After striving for so long, I have not been able to convey a single matter plainly to you. Then why do you come here and put on these charades for me? I am speaking from my own experience. To those unfamiliar with me, this might seem like a novel revelation. However, this is not new to me. Nor is anything I have said new to those who know me. Understand this. Be aware that you are imposing and piling up a massive negative karma upon these children. This is all I have to say. This is all I felt like saying today. What can be done? It suffocates my mind. There is no other recourse. Today, I have spoken words I have never uttered before. You must bear them in mind. There is pain. It is solely out of pain that I have spoken. Now you understand, don't you? I have spoken because my mind is overwhelmed. Think for yourselves. With the disposition of not letting go of what is in your grasp while simultaneously grasping for what is above, you can never truly prosper. Let what must go, go. If you can preserve it as a memory, it is a time ordained for you by God. Accomplish it. Regarding that, you have been advised numerous times. This is how it is; we must act and fulfill it. What we are demonstrating now through our actions are its negative repercussions. Let that conclude and pass. Let it end with your lifetime. Not just countless times, but I have spoken to an extent that defies expression. Yet, not only do you fail to absorb any of it, you do not even accord it the slightest respect. What was said might be incomprehensible to newcomers. However, everyone who knows me understands exactly what I have stated. You do as you will. If you do good, it is good. If you do ill, it is ill. I have nothing further to add. Because my mind is suffocating. By repeatedly speaking to you, my mind feels profoundly stifled. I am unable to accomplish anything.
Guruvani
Birthday Poojitha Dedication Edition - 2006
Modernized Life and Yoga

We have been taught that Kali is bad. Kali is never bad. Each quality has its own corresponding nature. So, once we understand this, what we need to develop from it is our children. This is what you do not know. What to do? Didn't I say, four tuitions for four children. In one house. That kept increasing and increasing, and then one person got two or three tuitions. Isn't it needed? What are we going to do with these children after teaching them like this? Out of a hundred who study like this, ten will get into some small job. All the rest are just spreading anarchy here. If you are ready to say no to this, I have nothing to say. Right or wrong? Because of a lack of this, he will go somewhere else looking for a job from here. Then going there, or getting a job from there, living right there, then coming home one day a year for Onam and Christmas with a card. Sometimes bringing a lot of things and dumping them at home, feeling awkward for two days, and there he goes. Isn't this what is modernized? So it is not this. The time we got is good. What did I say now? We have been taught that this yoga is good. It is good. If we attach our soul to it without looking at what quality is in our soul, by then we will see some comfort and relief. Again, after a few days, if the mind does not stay with it, it will turn into a pain. How do we change this pain? It is a pain for the mind. At the same time, in this house, our children and wife or other siblings will not understand this either. Tell me, what will we do there? This is where we fail. Isn't it right? It is not like that. You have faith in God or love. It is true. It is good. If our children and this woman do not understand this as well, it is a danger. No matter what is done, what does the mother of these children say? "Here he comes, what is it here now? You didn't clean there, you didn't clean here, you didn't do that," this is what he will be saying. "It's enough if he just takes off his head and leaves from here," if said loud enough for these children to hear, wouldn't it be quite bad? Do these children need anything else to go bad? Most houses are in this state. It is just that it is in various ways. So we must escape from this. This is what I have to say.
