If you are becoming family people, what you need is the complete success of the family. How is that? If the children do not stand with us, we cannot do anything for them. When each of them becomes householders--whether male or female, they will become householders, won't they. They will act according to their minds and get ruined. Nothing can be done. So, having understood this, it is about how we will straighten this out through our lives. You should think about this. You cannot do anything else. That is not to tell you to take sannyasa (renunciation). You do not need to take sannyasa. We can take sannyasa when we need it. We do not need sannyasa. What we need is the survival of our country. Do we need it or not? While the country survives, through that course of action, we should acquire children in the path of dharma who acquire merit. There is no use saying any other justification. This is not going to just come running. Otherwise, will it work if you just bathe saying it is sannyasa, and say it is good, not bad, it is fine? I didn't say this to say all that. It is for that. Yoga is good, not saying it is bad. Then it will lead to actions that the house cannot comply with. Understood? In the old days, some of my old people used to say--my father was like a sannyasi. Mother was like that. They do not know what they gained with all this. So we do this action for our gain. Because our soul will spend only a very short time with this body. We carry this around bathed and covered. Once this is gone, this soul will fly and reach somewhere. Won't it? What will it go into?
Disciple: It will go to the nearest solar system.
Guru: It will go closer and closer there. Right?
Disciple: It will go to whichever one nearby provides the most love through prayer.

Guru: It will go there. Once it goes there, it is certain that this life will stay there. Do you understand? Don't we hold onto something, like a goddess or a god? The question is what we will become if we call out like that and merge into it. Now, I am saying the opposite to you where you are seated. Right? Is it or not? If you go to a yogi or a sanyasi, is this how they speak! They will take up other matters and speak, won't they? So, for us, it is not that. Shouldn't our father and mother come to the right maturity? Otherwise, will it work if we blame them or blame each other? This is your family life. Fostering this, growing through us, growing into the children, it then grows into the society. These children are the custodians of that society. And then of the nation. It is my belief that without understanding this, you will not earn any dignity through your family life. I do not know what else to say. We must think about the dynamics of life and respect it. That is growth. The merit of life is the fortune within this. You are being told to bring merit to this life. How should you take that? Now, food is given to the father or mother. Girls must be very careful about that. It is given to the husband. She gives it as if giving it to God in her belief. But not that he is God. Why is it given like that? I only spoke of those who have belief. I didn't speak of the others. Why give it like that? We give to others out of love too, don't we? It is not that. If given to this person like this, there will be a change in his blood. This is its real aspect. So, this has been told to you first. Was it told or not? Why is this? One must ensure that the life does not get blood impurities due to aging. If more sorrow comes, what will happen? Do you know? Blood pressure will occur. Similarly, if this blood does not remain in a balance, things will not work out. It will lean towards something. Some mothers are doing it now. Looking at the little ones, they are nice and chubby and plump. Isn't it so? Only if they are plump like this, can we make them walk when we see them. So, by giving unwanted things to this child like this, the marrow will increase. That will harm his character. Whether a girl or a boy, it will. All these westerners are like that. Their tendencies are being brought here and passed on by the mother and father together. How bad this is. Why say this, to mock you? It is being passed on. We cannot do anything about this. Now, there are people of your age who are very worried, wondering what I will do when these children grow up. We see it like that for most people. If it is wrong, you must say it is wrong. Then, seeing this new model nowadays, there will be a little more sorrow. What is it? Isn't there an old age home near your place? It seems there isn't in Palakkad. You are ignorant people. You have no information. Shouldn't a place be made to take the father and mother somewhere and accommodate them? Why are you doing this ignorant act? Where to take and abandon the father and mother? When they get old, shouldn't they be taken somewhere and locked in a room? It is only now understood that there is an old age home for that. Shouldn't there be? We are going to take them and leave them in this center. Didn't you understand? After some more time, when you get old, these children will learn and do the same thing. Now, what do foreigners do if the father lies dead? These artists--they know. Tell me this! You at least act out this art. How would it be if such an art is practiced? Wouldn't we be totally confused? Not that. The elder has died. So what to do--find a good hotel, have a meal, and go there! Now you understand. Just act that out. We need to gain through them. Because if they at least act like this, we can go on for ten days. So this is being pinched and peeled. It is understood since how long the injustice of our country has started. Haven't we come doing divine worship? To this day, no one knows where this karma started and where it ended. Because of that, what the father showed the son, and what the mother showed the daughter, and then when they entered the realm of modernization, this and that got mixed up and became nothing, they are children without wealth. If we say we will bring them merit, he will not stay anywhere around there in that manner. He will run away. An example for that, if we bring these boys who walk all along this way, and keep them at home, they will have some common decency ٹ Give them oil and everything, clean them up and see. How many days will they stay, with us? If he stays, he will run away after two or four days. He likes to lie in this street. So, understanding this, what should we do. So, even where this sanyasa is spoken of, this danger exists, and where Grihasthashrama is spoken of, this danger exists. How do we escape from here? Just say what you know. That is, we should understand something like this. Our karma and dharma that have come till today, and the mistakes that have happened to us over time--the spiritual being wants him to see this with his own eyes. Let that be. Shouldn't common people at least have an imagination of this? Otherwise, he will say harsh things keeping these children around too. These children will become like that. Isn't it so? So the mother and father must be completely exemplary to us. Along with that, we say the Guru who gives us education now. Or let it be the one who gives. All these are called Guru, Guru. All that is true. But shouldn't we know what qualities our spiritual guru should have? What is it? There is a path that many people whom we call our men of action have taken. The Guru's karma is to steer us back along this path. You ask. Even if told, wouldn't you understand?
Disciple: Are the paths taken by our ancestors the right ones?

Guru: We have merely heard and assumed that they are good paths. That is not what I am asking you. Must we not observe all that our ancestors have done? Is it sufficient to look only at the good? If we look solely at the good, we will be unable to bear it. Do you understand? If we bring in only that goodness, there will be no one even in our own homes to accept it. Then what can be said about the rest of the world? Must we not understand it in this manner? We are incapable of it. We are currently standing at that very point of incapability. We must consider what solution we should seek for this. The path to change this is what is called the *Guru*. Do you understand? Then what is that path? We must observe the total actions (*karmas*) of those who have come thus far, the ancestors (*pitrus*), and the karma of their worship ranging from the Goddesses and Gods to even the demons. This is the Guru; nothing else. Education, wealth, and capability—we can find these everywhere in the world. This, however, cannot be obtained so easily. The subsequent thought is how to obtain it. We can only receive it in accordance with our own capacity, can we not? We must acquire it by closely acquainting ourselves with it, to the extent of our capacity. Thus, it takes ten to twelve years just to understand a single inherent tendency (*vasana*) of the Guru. It is not possible otherwise. What if you say you can rush in and grab it right now! "I have received the initiation, I have received the other!" So, all his impurities are gone because he received the initiation, right? He is completely unaware that these impurities are actually being uprooted. Do you understand? Now, let us consider someone as a Guru, or whatever lump of earth. Must we not struggle for at least twelve years to stir and comprehend his true nature? Only after stirring and observing this can we determine whether this person is good or bad. What is being said is that you should not hastily grab and hold on tightly simply because something is proclaimed to be good. This is what was mentioned earlier. Our ancestors have passed on in this manner. Do not go that way—do what you can. The virtues and vices of our life-force (*jiva*), what we observe—that is what is meant by 'seeing'. Therefore, what we observe here is the antiquity of our *jiva*. It is neither male nor female. It is the antiquity of the *jiva*. Otherwise, no matter how much we speak or listen, it is of no avail. Thus, this antiquity of the *jiva* is the process of realizing the myriad qualities of the Guru. That is its reality. How can one know that? This is categorized into *Jagrat* (waking), *Swapna* (dreaming), *Sushupti* (deep sleep), and *Turiya* (the fourth state of consciousness). It is in this *Turiya* that we perceive our Guru. When perceived in that manner, one must also understand that this is the antiquity of our *jiva*. Why is it explained in this way? You do not comprehend this. These are all intimately familiar to you. Now, we must descend to the lowest level, step by step, lower and lower. That state of our *jiva* must undergo a transformation. At that time, numerous negative elements will accompany us. Why is that? If we intend to do something good, our mind impulsively leaps across to the other shore of the ocean. What can be done? This is precisely what the Guru is for. If he is told that he cannot go, come, or stand in such a manner, what is he supposed to do? According to the principles of Yoga, it is stated thus. Who is forbidden from residing in the house where a Yogi lives? The mother is forbidden. Is the mother not a woman? Suppose he just proceeds in that manner, what has he achieved? When you say you have lived for so long, shouldn't I question you? That is why I am asking. What has he attained?
Disciple: It has become like building a wall.

Guru: We cannot do anything. We cannot even demolish this wall. The Guru exists to demolish this wall. Do you understand now? I am explaining this in a way that you can understand, without resorting to complex *Vedanta*. This is not *Vedanta*; it is pure knowledge. It is about how our Guru is situated within the realm of this knowledge. Even if we struggle, we can only comprehend this by offering love. Otherwise, the Guru cannot be attained in such a manner. When we talk about giving love, this Guru will exhibit all forms of love as well as all sorts of irrationalities.
Guruvani
Birthday Commemorative Edition - 2006
How can one deny the truth of nature?

We have behind us a familiarity that has come through worshipping, seeing, knowing, and speaking as many *Yugadharmas*. Having come thus through many ages, it is now written that someone did penance for ten thousand years. Can that happen in one lifetime? It speaks of a course of karma accumulated through penance over numerous lifetimes. Someone ended up attaining the position of a demon. Thus, how many crores do you think comprise the countless thirty-three crore deities mentioned by Hindus up to this day? We have traversed through the karmas of so many aeons! Speaking of one *Yuga* or a *Chaturyuga*, it is an exceptionally vast calculation. A *Manvantara* is described as consisting of seventy-one such *Chaturyugas*. Having passed six such *Manvantaras*, this is the seventh *Manvantara*. Thus, the residual karma resulting from actions—seen and heard, known and unknown—across all these *Manvantaras* stands captured like an image in this atmosphere. Do you believe that? It is the truth. Has nature captured a photograph of us sitting here, talking, and discussing today or not? You must not say that what we need to observe here is non-existent. It exists. That which does not exist has no name. There must be something that someone has discovered up to this day. That is why we have given it a name and brought it forward in this manner. Thus, we lived, grew, and perished within the concept of that name. The past karmas are behind us. Do you believe that? Did we not have ancestors who worshipped and caused others to worship using a name? Should you not consider whether they and the entities they worshipped still exist behind us? Therefore, when our ancestors were born here, there was a karma—tendencies shaped by their minds, capabilities, and actions even before birth—that dissolved into their blood, flesh, and marrow. I am asking if you have any doubt that a portion of that karma is inherited by our own *jiva*. So, how can we discard this? There are countless things your parents, ancestors, or elders logically learned, taught, and discussed. But it is not any of this. Is there not a separate karma that remains from the times we, in our ignorance, called out, made others call out, and acted knowingly or unknowingly? Where will this go? The rationalist went this way, the liberation-seeker went that way. Let them be. Leaving both of them aside, there are a number of people caught in between, aren't there? Where will they go? Is there not a realm where I, you, and others have come and acted? I am asking whether we have the authority to claim that this does not exist. The question is, how can we deny this truth of nature, which has permeated as individual atoms of the karma that has come and gone before and behind us? It certainly exists in nature, doesn't it? So, shouldn't we observe what exists? Speak in a way you understand. This is not rationalism. You should not misunderstand it as such. I am trying to impart my experience to you. This is not just empty rhetoric. It can be seen. That is experience. I am placing your own children before you. I did not bring them from my home, did I? They are standing right here now, aren't they? So, I am showing this to you by making them speak from within you. I am saying this after observing it. I am explaining that this is the very cause of our disease. That is, haven't our ancestors and we ourselves passed away after worshipping and performing both good and bad deeds? Our body is a manifestation of karma originating from the natural pleasures of their souls. How can one render this non-existent? Our primary question is whether you have seen this or not.
Disciple: I have.

Guru: How, then, are we to comprehend this? I am articulating this in a manner comprehensible to you. I am going to share one of my own experiences with you. For instance, consider Narayana Guru, Sri Shankara, and Chattampi Swami—they were all born in Kerala itself. Consciously or unconsciously, numerous individuals place their faith in them. Does not this faith, along with the karma that engendered it, persist? The pertinent question is whether or not we ought to apprehend this karma. Similarly, having observed the entire world in this manner, there is a necessity for an individual to draw all of this closer to us. What kind of individual should that be?
Disciple: It must be a Guru.
Guru: Yes. It must be a Guru. Is it not the Guru who created all this? Therefore, all this is indeed the Guru. The Guru exists in everything.
Disciple: A Guru endowed with spiritual wisdom.

Guru: Yes. When speaking of spirituality, what we have heard and seen—as I mentioned earlier—is the kind of spirituality demonstrated by most people. But rejecting that, the person must be an individual who desires to transmit that karma to us, having comprehended the philosophy in detail and recognized the damages involved. Only such an individual can articulate it. Would it be correct to distance someone because they are a woman or draw someone close because they are a man? So, it is evident that we have not even considered what rights our women possess, haven't we? Our mother, another's wife, another's daughter, another's sister—do you believe or not that all these mothers have faced this danger? Speak. Let anyone among you speak. For me to instruct you, you will only understand if you inquire. Otherwise, if you claim, "I am a rationalist, no one will come to my house," then I have nothing to say. This is not merely for our human world, nor just for the celestial realm, nor only for the masculine world; the Guru who elucidates the realms of this solar system, encompassing all described planes, is the one who restores this to us. Have you understood? If not, I shall explain. That is why I am asking. You must comprehend it thoroughly. You are youngsters. If you go somewhere, merge your time with this ignorance, and return as the possessor of regrettable karma, what am I to do?

Are we not seeking to become owners of a wretched karma that voluntarily embraces blindness? How shall we alter this? If we transmit this to our children, if we declare the existence or non-existence of what has been transmitted to them thus far, what are they to make of it? You must comprehend this. I shall not inquire of you regarding that which does not exist. I shall only ask about that which exists. I shall solely recount how I have perceived that which exists. You need not harbor any doubts. You must attain this conviction. Otherwise, if I speak and it is deemed incorrect—if you assume I am merely speaking at random, have I not utterly failed? Only if you believe can I elucidate an aspect of it to you. You do believe, do you not? It is because I am unwell that I am exerting such effort to convey this to you. Why am I, who am so unwell, telling you this? You must grasp that. From a ghoul to the realm referred to as 'Vethala Nagaram', teaching us the nature of a Vethala, then leaving that realm and ascending back to the celestial realm (Deva Bhumika), leaving the celestial realm and proceeding to the realm of sages (Rishi Mandala), and from the realm of sages moving towards the formless realm, there stands a natural truth in this atmosphere that demonstrates how the realm of forms exists or does not exist. Does it make any difference if you, I, or anyone else claims it exists or does not exist? When we believe that all of this exists, do we not require a nature here that shows us its primordial form, the cause of its destruction, the various elements through which destruction occurred, and where, when, and how that trajectory of karma persisted? Should we not place our faith in this? Will we not attain an experience from it only when we believe that there is a truth in what we believe and act accordingly? Why am I telling you this now? I am stating this for a specific purpose. Understanding the blunders that may ensue if we do not tread that path, having imparted all these blunders to the children growing up before us, we will perish in ignorance. This deceased aggregation then brings forth souls conditioned by this dissonance into the nature that emerges as the children of our children. If you contend that this is not the case, then there is no point in my speaking. We are born and raised in this atmosphere, and we shall depart, leaving it behind. So, how were we in our childhood? How have we become now? How will we be after a while? We are witnessing all this changing ourselves. Thus, your inquiry is whether or not this Truth-Substance, which has manifested through so many countless births in this nature in various permutations, exists, and if it exists, what is it? Therefore, the states of waking (Jagrat), dreaming (Swapna), and deep sleep (Sushupti) that revealed this "what"—just as we perceived it in the waking state, similarly in the dreaming and deep sleep states—from where did you attain the knowledge that you slept well? It is the comfort attained by our body and a tranquility attained by the life-force that has conveyed this. Is it not? Thus, it has convinced us even though we were asleep. If someone asks, 'Get lost, how can you, who lay asleep yesterday, claim this?', what can he possibly answer? Is this something we displayed? This is not mere rationalism. Is it not a pragmatic argument of existence? We must perceive at least this argument of what exists. Later, we can examine the argument of what does not exist. Is what I am saying correct or incorrect? Therefore, having perceived the argument of what exists, let catching hold of what does not exist be reserved for later. We shall grasp it. We can grasp the non-existent as well. Standing firm in the karma that declares all of this indeed exists, one must analyze and comprehend each of these distinctly. Through whom should we comprehend this? I am not speaking under the assumption that all of you know. However, everyone can listen to it being told. Some within our consciousness know. That it exists, that this is the truth, that there is something else beyond this. Only if you believe in this manner can I elucidate these matters to you thus. Should I proceed further only if you believe all these things I have stated? Consequently, there is within us the knowledge and ignorance of countless souls whose practices our ancestors either followed or neglected. Is there not? Equipped with this, we are going to discern what exists from what does not. This currently is non-existent. It is something to be discarded; hence, all of this is an illusion (Maya). Having proclaimed that everything is the Maya of the Lord, why can't the one who preaches this Vedanta simply chop off his own body? Is this not non-existent? Then why is he carrying around this malodorous body, bathing it, dressing it, and covering it? Yet he can claim he has nothing to do. Cannot he? I ask, where will this scholar and the ignoramus, who split syllables, interpret, chant 'Soham', and make us believe, end up? What is the point of my saying something without this being understood? Let us consider a human being whom we believe in. Give it any name you wish. Must we not attain an experiential realization functioning with his life and body, brought about by the spiritual merit of this human being, whether he learned it or not, whether he knew it or not? I will not claim that this can be shown to all of you. Because it was already mentioned how our ancestors proceeded in this manner. Thus, as a continuation of this, the remaining consequence of our being born, raised, and dying at some point is our current presence here. We must desire and bring forth what should emerge in this life-force and rectify the plight of this life-force.
Guruvani
Birthday Commemorative Dedication Edition - 2006
That which is known in the witness of Waking, Dreaming, and Deep Sleep

We need a spiritual body that eliminates the misfortunes of our life; each one of us needs it. If you say this does not exist, I will not speak to you. Thus, we must observe the body where the soul resided, the body that perished, and the body that flourished. That refers to the waking (*Jagrat*), dreaming (*Swapna*), and deep sleep (*Sushupti*) states, or the past, present, and future. Must we not be able to understand that this is an action intrinsically connected to our life? This is what I am asking you. Asceticism (*Sanyasa*) is not mere talk. You should not assume that all of this is strictly meant for asceticism. Every one of you, as family householders, should evolve to this level and transform into the greatest performer of duties, the most righteous being, and a powerhouse of action brimming with immense glory. If not, there is no point in my saying anything further. Therefore, shouldn't you understand what exists while you are still alive, and within that understanding, realize what we and God—or that word—truly are, and ultimately accept it as our Guru? Speak up if you have any doubts. Not everyone can grasp everything. It will only resonate with and be useful to certain individuals. We need someone of that nature to be our Guru.

This is precisely what we were taught about Krishna through the phrase '*Yatra yatra Yogeshwara Krishna*'. Having learned this, if we are to realize its truth in both waking and dreaming states, we require a spiritual Guru by our side. You must trace and extract from the karmic record inscribed in your own life how that person's actions have progressed—whether they went wrong, possessed flaws, lacked flaws, or aligned with the truth. The Guru is the one who imparts this profound knowledge. There is no point in offering any other justification for this. A testament to this in our recent epoch—that is, someone born in the middle of this Kali Yuga before its full onset—is Sri Krishna. We must carefully observe everything that unfolded through Sri Krishna. If all those events transpired through Sri Krishna, then why did he undertake such a massive and exhausting journey? That is to say, didn't he travel across the entirety of our Bharat? Running alongside the five Pandavas, crossing from here to another shore, and from there managing to build Dwaraka. Is that not our history? It was after building Dwaraka that he fell, struck by an arrow—which is sometimes attributed to a hunter's prowess; whatever it may be, he collapses. It was precisely then that he told the very disciple who had achieved and facilitated so many victories, 'Arjuna, take at least these women and children and transport them safely to the mainland.' I ask you, what is the underlying trickery of these scholars who, instead of explaining this to us and guiding us correctly, impose upon us an inexperienced illusion (*Mayavilasa*) by reciting all this? To speak authoritatively about the author of the Gita, shouldn't a scholar possess absolute faith? Furthermore, if you begin dismissing it by claiming, "it is not this, it is not this"! What have you become through this nihilistic philosophy? The entire anxiety of your mind dissolved into emptiness, and you yourself became empty. If any rationalist wishes to deny it, let him do so. Can he be guided anywhere other than the path his own mind dictates? This is the fallacy he commits, either knowingly or unknowingly. This is not what I am conveying to you. A trajectory of karma—spanning billions of years in which our ancestors, knowingly or unknowingly, worshipped, caused others to worship, abstained, were born, and died—permeates this very atmosphere. Have you not understood that it is a distinct, inherent power hidden and dissolved within the air, fire, water, sand, and dust? Do you have any doubts? The Guru who materializes and reveals this to us is God. By demonstrating how it is formed, how it resided in the earth, how it existed in the sky, how it was in the water, and how it manifested in the five elements; recognizing the five elements as the five senses, where did these five sheaths (*Panchakoshas*) operate within the vast spectrum of these five senses that we came to comprehend through smell, touch, and sight? What is it? Is there anything lacking in this? Even if I claim there is nothing, you should not simply agree. That is exactly why I am asking. It is not easy for us to merely sit, ponder, and fully grasp this. The intrinsic inclination of our life force is not that immense. Therefore, if we are to be shown the errors and truths witnessed yesterday, we require a foundational stone. That is the spiritual stone (*Athmashila*). '*Atmanatmaniveditam*'—we need a remnant of action where the soul is offered unto the soul. We cannot attain this except through Him. If our language assigns such a form and articulates it, it possesses a specific name in that respective language. It is sufficient to understand it in that manner. Stating whether we exist or not cannot induce any true emptiness. Thus, our theoretician is the Guru who makes us directly experience this. You must witness a profound action where this Guru, having observed the events that transpired through waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, amalgamates what currently exists with what is yet to come, and seamlessly imparts it into our life.

I stated this at the very beginning. Not everyone, but a select few may perceive this as the truth. By understanding this, we must recognize the hardships, glory, respect, humility, wickedness, and righteousness inherent in our own lives. Isn't that so? It is there that one must truly understand what one's Guru is. You must definitively decide whether you want this or not. Therefore, if we are to draw closer to this essential realization we desire, do we not also require the experiential familiarity to observe where the snow transformed into rain, solidified into ice, melted back into water, and ultimately, where it reached?

Where was it in the ancient times? Without anyone making it, this snow was present here. This is the brilliance of nature. Then it melted as snow, and to be cut away, it became hard enough and it melted and thus the water body rose. It rose through the water body and became water itself. Whatever it had to mix with, it mixed and there is a story where it submerged Dwarka. So it is about that state. Such a great man, that is why a Guru is needed. By denying the Guru, if any matters are spoken at any time, that matter is gone. Then it cannot be retrieved. If one thinks of getting it through that logic! The one who is sitting in the tragic state of not being able to recognize his own father, how can he analyze this logically? Only if I talk a lot of nonsense like this will you understand. Did the mother say it was the father, or did the father say it was the father? So couldn't this just be said normally? In this state, how else can I scold you? Right or wrong? This is what happens in my house. I don't know what happens in your house. So, because of the familiarity of such a pathetic acquaintance itself, we must believe that there is a lack of knowledge in us. Thus, maintaining this ignorance, and pointing out that it doesn't exist, the Guru brings us to that extent. At the time of our birth, we were not familiarized by being told about such matters. What we have heard and kept is what our father, mother, and ancestors have said--isn't a vision of God enough? It is on the outside of this specific ignorance that we stand. Not a hundred of these. Even if a thousand appear, we gain nothing. Even if a crore appear, nothing happens. The one who makes us capable of offering our soul through the soul is the true spiritual Guru. If you have any doubt, you can ask. You must know it. That is why I am saying this. Do not go with doubts. Now, didn't I see yesterday; I slept well yesterday, I felt very good last night, sleep; isn't there a lack of knowledge communicated in our hands like this? So now I told someone else that I slept well yesterday. If I say I didn't experience it, what will we do? Isn't it I who knows whether I slept or not? So the feeling of 'I' is there. That 'I' is what saw everything, existing in a form not different from oneself, with the nature of evolution, the dharma existing in this literal nature, the action of the form of this sound. Should we get back this humility or not? That is, this sound we hear mutually now, do you realize that it has merged into this atmosphere or not? Just like that, is there any doubt that this nature took a photo of all of us sitting and talking together? Just like this, our ancestors worshiped and made others worship, mixing the bad and the good, true worship and the untrue reality, shouldn't we realize this? A remnant of the life that acted mingled and forgotten, known and unknown for so long, is this life sticking to my body, shouldn't we know this? Or shouldn't we? So this knowledge can only be gained through the Guru. So whichever deity or whichever demon is seen, my Guru must be there. What is the doubt? You must ask about the part you have a doubt. Only then can I say. If I make you mature through my words and make you ask, what can I do? Shouldn't you be the one in need? So, if one says this is not it, this is not it--if a toddy seller is given the water from old gruel, will it become toddy? Its color will somewhat match. So milk is white, this is also white. And then there is a slight difference in their form changes. Shouldn't we distinguish this? So it is about this matter that needs to be known that we are asking. This cannot be known unless our house is right. If one becomes a Guru like this, who goes along with every rowdyism and every good thing by habit, how would it be? When I say this, you will think, alas, did he say that about the Guru? This is how the Guru is. A complete rogue. So whatever rogue behaviour is seen, I see my Guru along with it. Why does one say it should be seen like this? Thus, it is the path the Guru passed through that we are shown. When the Guru and that seen form dissolve together, as to what one becomes, fourthly if it is this one--take and place it. Then showing us an amorphous nature in this nature of what stands dissolved and undissolved, in this formless being, one must show us as true law what resides in it. The item without form. Through this formless being what was done? If we do not see this through the Guru too, how will you see it? It won't happen. For this, you need a Guru. What kind of Guru should it be? Only if good things are heard, will the Guru sit there. If bad things are heard, the Guru will leave. If bad things are seen or heard, the Guru will run away from there. Then who will separate the bad and the good from you? If there is any space for that, tell me. A formless power that knows and informs that your mind is not lost or corrupted and not bad in another way, shouldn't you see it as a form in yourself? He is formless. But he is formed. Through whatever that formed being went--this too is being shown to us. That is waking state, dream ṭ 'whatever was seen in the waking state' in dream and then in deep sleep, and after that the special quality of these form differences and name differences is what Turiya, Turiyaateetam show. Waking, dreaming, deep sleep, Turiya, Turiyaateetam; turning us around with these five parts, the skill in action is the Guru. During the time of the deity, what was the deity, what did the sage do there, that sage who is called the doer of action, yogi, knowledgeable one, devotee--turned in four ways who are these sages, what is the connection between this sage and my Guru? Or how do those good qualities of all the past deities reside in my Guru? Like saying this Shakteam, Shaivam, Vaishnavam, singing with a thousand hands and showing a role, we call it Bhadra. But shouldn't we see the true quality of Durga? Recognizing the qualities of this life without gender distinction is our Guru's acquaintance. If one says this is not it, I have nothing to say. I can go from here. What do you say? This must come into our experience. That is what I said, I am not training the children brought from my house for this. This is being trained on your children, your husband, and your wife. This is the love of trust in the Guru that flows through you to your children, and from those children to their children, to an enduring state, showing what was there and what wasn't, being poured into you. Say yes or no. But this is all I have to say. Everything stands strong in this nature at a formless place where one's Guru takes it and shows it. It is this Guru who characterizes what that constant power of the past era is, and by making us know it, goes forward again. This cannot be done by the deity. The deity will show some rolling and manipulation. This is not some manipulation and rolling. Shouldn't we know what the evolutionary theory of our life force is by seeing it and knowing through what all we have crawled and climbed up? Isn't it through your soul that you have to see it? So the soul sitting along with the life force in this body, the knowledge that is known by reflecting both, isn't it true knowledge? The question is whether you believe there is a soul and a life force in us itself. If we do not have in front of us an action path to retrieve it and show it in ourselves, we will wander bewildered anywhere. Understand this from experience. This <span200>is belief.</span200>

Let us tell only the Guru, and no one else, about what we experience in the waking, dream, and deep sleep states. Why am I seeing so much bad? Why am I seeing so much good? How wayward am I? Why have I been placed in this seat of ignorance? — The Guru is the authority to ask such questions. Now, what is the doubt? Do you believe it or not?
Disciple: I believe.
Guru: Believe like that. Here it is, how did you feel after applying the sacred ash?
Disciple: It was better.

Guru: When we take some medicine, doesn't it aggravate in another way instead of subsiding? How did you feel when you applied this sacred ash? It subsided. So, who is the sorcerer here? It is our faith. Transcending all this, it is a self-offering that unites one's life and breath. Not to spout great Vedanta or say it was like this in the Kathopanishad; I am not talking nonsense. Is their experience what is written down? I did not say that to deny or interpret any of it. There is no need to interpret anything here. It is what it is. If it is not convenient for you, learn it from somewhere else, or take it, boil it, and eat it. That is all. When I say this, you will not like me. Why? I am an unlearned man, one who does nothing, and a great trickster. After explaining so much trickery, what a disgrace it is to call me an unlearned trickster. I am stating both together. 'Jagrat swapna sushuptinam sakshimurthy namonamah' — Guru is the karma sustained by our household, myself, and one's lineage, encompassing what we have worshipped as a witness in this, what we have failed to worship, the bad, the evil, the good, what we experienced knowingly or unknowingly, and what came by special destiny.
Guruvani
Birthday Tribute Edition - 2006
The Guru speaking to the devotees from Palakkad.

Take Palakkad for instance. The problem seen there is the result of what they have been worshipping, believing it to be a good path. The difficulty we might face by worshipping in such a way is that it will stagnate within our life. They will not respect anything. They will not step forward to do anything. Consequently, their children will grow up with wealth, riches, and enjoyment. But these children will fall into danger. They do not realize this. There are many such households. This problem exists in every house that shows off such arrogance. Aren't they flaunting their wealth and authority? It is present in all these houses. Nothing can be done about it. This is because of the mistakes that occurred in this outdated system of worship. Now we have faith. Can we avoid proceeding with that faith? We cannot change that fact. Then how should it be? We must investigate it like this. If we continue doing this for eight, ten, fifteen, or twenty years, the very course of this life will turn into that. Right? If it goes on like this, we will end up being ignorant of yoga, karma, devotion, or any other path of knowledge. One must understand this first. Otherwise, we will be in trouble. It is good. Everything is good. But then, if a little education, wealth, and authority come into our house, they will not respect anyone. They will simply lack a respectful nature. When will they eventually return? It will be in their old age, when they are entirely fed up with these children. Then they will start crying out, 'Oh God, Oh God, Oh God'. There will be no saving them. These children will scatter in different directions. This is the entire situation in Palakkad. Ah, did you see them? A nest of Ezhuthachans. Isn't there a community of people called Ezhuthachans there? Most of them suffer from mental deficiencies.
Disciple: It is there in many families.

Guru: Will the locals believe it if I say this now? This is not what I am saying. You remember what I told you when we came here that day. That innate tendency (vasana) will not enter their life. If the vasana does not manifest in life, we cannot grasp it. Consequently, many youths are simply wasting away on this path. When this happens among the youth, one group takes that trajectory. Suppose there are five members in our household. Three or four of them are on different paths. One is on a virtuous path. These four will dislike him. Whether male or female, they stubbornly stand their ground amidst this chaos. We cannot make them obedient in any circumstance. Humility is simply not imparted. Their inner selves remain rigidly blocked. Therefore, if a transformation is to occur, shouldn't an action that engenders humility arise within us? What shall we do if this humility does not emerge? If we attempt to induce it forcefully, it will merely push them to the brink of destruction. Ultimately, we can never save that family. Then there is a faction devoted to rationalism and spiritual liberationism. They pose as significant figures in both ideologies. This is the prevalent observation throughout the Palakkad region, starting from Ottapalam. Thus, upon understanding this, one realizes that this is entirely the residue of deep-rooted vasanas. How can we transform this entrenched vasana? Even if one desires to do so, it cannot be changed. You must understand it in that manner. Why is it said that it will not change? You are all artists, aren't you? This artistic vasana remains with them even if they face failure; they will not abandon it. There are numerous such individuals. Many have been lost. Individuals who deviated like this in a family are reborn in a state influenced by an ancestral spirit that perished elsewhere. They will never deviate from that path. Simultaneously, there is one's inherent vasana, which will frequently surge forth. For instance, just as I mentioned regarding Ezhuthachan, there are countless petty writers. They are always humming and wandering about. How many such individuals have truly prospered? They cannot; they will not improve. Thus, observing this, we fail to comprehend the trajectory of our karma. None of you should harbor the illusion that we can progress without exhausting this karma. It will not happen. Wealth, capabilities, and prosperity may grace a generation, and they might live a commendable life. However, within them, the contemplation of the Divine may be present in some, while entirely absent in others. For some, it is quite different; they aspire to become sheer brutes. It continues like this. Despite possessing intellect and ability, they veer off in this direction. I am asking you how this can be resolved. You should perceive what I am saying as reflecting the ignorance of your mind. Shouldn't I express it? It is inappropriate for me to conceal this truth. It is like chanting 'Narayana' only until crossing the bridge, and then reverting to the old ways. Such is the state of the mind. I am explaining this so that you do not have to suffer in the end due to a lack of understanding. If you approach me, I will speak only in this manner. I do not seek your affection. What do I require? I desire the magnificence of your spiritual growth. If you are to attain that greatness, you cannot proceed in this manner. I am merely explaining its nature. What is occurring now? Take the children of officers here; if there are four children, all four are sent for tuition! Why is that? If a single mark is lost, the mother's mind becomes agitated, akin to moss gathered and stuffed into a basket. If moss is packed tightly into a basket, it ferments and generates intense heat, doesn't it? Her mind burns similarly. This is improper. Some women come and lament, 'I have nine children, Swami. Seven of them are officers, both boys and girls. But two children—what can be done? One daughter failed a section and tried three times with no success.' Did they lie? No. 'No matter what the other child does, there is no progress.' What does this signify? There are wonderful children in this house. Many have secured employment. Yet, she is a mother incapable of teaching them the true essence of life, do you understand? She provides milk, serves food, washes their clothes, and refuses to let the children do any chores. When situations demand it, these children—some of whom are quite unruly—will wander down whatever path they please. Rather than letting them face consequences, the parents quickly cover it up, pamper them, and cater to their whims, don't they? I am pointing out the mischievous folly committed by such parents. What will be their state when they grow up? This represents the household. You will find yourselves utterly helpless. This is the consequence of pursuing various misguided forms of devotion. You are unaware of it. This phenomenon is quite evident from Ottapalam onwards. You can verify this in every household. Consider the Brahmin streets; if there are twenty houses clustered together, you will undoubtedly find two widows there. What can be done?

Look at Ernakulam. The fundamental question is how we can comprehend all of this. Upon understanding it, regarding our ancestors—nobody deceived or destroyed anyone. It is an inherent misfortune residing within that soul. This soul will remain in such a state. You all assume, 'We are Grihasthashramis (householders); we are simply surviving somehow.' To be a true Grihasthashrami, unless they cultivate complete wisdom, prosperity, and competence, they will end up begging after one thing or another. What does this mean? What are your thoughts on this? This supplication should not exist. A Grihasthashrami implies a person who possesses the capability to lead their household and community in a pure and righteous manner. That is why it is said that society requires wealthy individuals, affluent people; otherwise, a place devoid of noble souls (sadhukkal) is considered desolate. What is meant by 'noble souls'?
Disciple: Those who correct errors upon observing them.
Guru: Exactly. If an error is spotted and corrected, shouldn't they rectify their course? What is the method for that?
Disciple: Humility is essential.

Guru: That humility is not present in his father, is it? Then what is he to do? Furthermore, our mothers have another trait. Speaking with great authority, they say, 'Narayana, God will take care of all that.' What is it? Haven't they entrusted it to God? Mother and father live like this in nature, living with all their character flaws and whatever else they have accumulated, and then for a few days, they will fervently call out to God. Then they will say, 'I have done whatever I needed to. If you want, you do it. I can't anymore.' Then there is a mother with even more knowledge than that. What is that? 'I gave birth to ten. I experienced such and such sorrows. You gave birth to one or two and became like this. What am I to do?' That is a kind of knowledge. You are getting the mother's knowledge in a solid form. Isn't that enough? When they became modernized, they won't even say that. See? The others would at least say that much. So, like that, the duty our mothers had to take up with humility was not given to them when they were little children. Did you understand what was said? Their mother and father raised them, got them married as best as they could, and they became children, children's children, husband and wife. Seeing this in many houses and seeing this English medium too, all of them got shaken and went another way. If you talk about a householder (Grihasthashrami), he is someone who should be an absolute model for this world. Otherwise, one should not wander like beggars and accept the householder stage. Then there is another thing shown, taking sannyasa (renunciation) at the time they are about to be destroyed and turned into ashes. They take the Bhagavatam and hum it, hum and study it for a few days, then they end up in a temple, then in a wayside inn. Now there are no wayside inns. That is a pity, isn't it? What is a wayside inn? In those days there were no vehicles or boats--if you go by boat, this thing won't work out. So they would pack their bags and set out. If they had to come to Thiruvananthapuram, they set out after packing their bags. They would sleep in these wayside inns and reach Thiruvananthapuram in ten days. So, we shouldn't just feel happy thinking about those times. It is all good for us. Now we don't need wayside inns. No roadside wells. No resting places for headloads. Do we? So we are born in a place where all these things are not needed. What did you understand? Life has become easy. So, I am telling you to look at that sorrow. If we had to deliver a thing to the town, look at the experience, difficulty, and trouble of those days. There is a hundred acres of land on the hill. Will you farm it and pick it up by hand? They do not understand the fact that things have become so easy now. You never even think like this. What to do? So, is the time we are born in better? Or is that better? The time we are born in is better. In the old days, if one house had education, the ten houses around it wouldn't have education. Do you know that? Suppose they get a letter in English. How will they read it? Then they have to walk somewhere for it. In the time of C. Kesavan and others, he was the 33rd B.A. holder in Travancore ٹ C. Kesavan and Sahodaran Ayyappan. We understood that it was only that much, didn't we? You can see that if you look at the Kochi souvenir.
Guruvani
September 2006

Right now, theology and all religious doctrines are being taught. Aren't there people who have studied this? Then why are you specifically teaching it now? Is it not because it cannot be put into practice here? How can it be attained by merely speaking of its valor? That is not possible. That great soul must come, grow, and grasp the history of that domain right from its beginning. After doing so, without giving that great soul their due, we cannot move forward. You do not understand this. We are taking responsibility for the errors that have crept into this prophetic religion. Thus, we are taking upon ourselves these two thousand four hundred and forty-four Gurus as well. After taking them, we must make them function. What did you understand from this? This is why seven generations have been mentioned, for them to come and act. Isn't that what I said when speaking about vision (darshan)? The time of all of them has passed. Whose time? That of all the successors. However, in this position, a few years of the Prophet (Nabi) still remain. I do not know if you have understood that. It has been one thousand five hundred years since he arrived. Only a few more days remain for that. The word spoken by that great soul must not be broken. Shouldn't they be capable of ensuring that word is not broken? But if the era of that great soul passes, then you will not be able to grasp it later. What is it? It must be grasped within this time frame itself. When we pray, we will connect with all the traditionally existing constellations of stars for that purpose. Different levels of importance are assigned to each one. After receiving this vision, it is being handed over to a Guru capable of bearing it. We must take it back ourselves. To practically implement it among the people through action, a distinct personality is required. Therefore, we must adopt the karma of this lineage of Gurus who have come and gone until now, right down to the 'Ustad'. Otherwise, if we go the other way, things will get complicated. It is the lack of time to grasp this that stands as a roadblock for Sri Krishna and the aforementioned Prophet. This is not something anyone can deny. It is a historical truth. This is not how the scholars put it. They are talking about some other convoluted theories. We must respect whoever has come and gone, wherever they may have been. We should not deny them. If we are not to deny them, we must embrace their karma. There is no other justification for it. We cannot proceed without clearing the path for them. That operates through the grace of God. So, if we attain a Guru or a guide, only when we reach that point and look from there can we see the rest. Therefore, it is like climbing a mountain. One must climb one, see its end, get down, and likewise climb up and down seven folds to accomplish the task. Narayana Guru gives many examples for this.
'There is medicine on the mountain, three snakes and
tigers standing guard on both its sides,
an outcaste took and consumed half of it,
it still shines, oh mind, you too take it!'

This is understood. But what to do? It did not come into this doctrine of karma. It is not enough to speak of the doctrine of dharma. The doctrine of karma must come. This is what is called experiential realization. When that realization later enters the realm of utilization, upon attaining it, we can only say that we have attained it. But it becomes true knowledge only when it is utilized for the people. Calling it a vision (darshan), they recite Vedantic hymns—their stance is that the vision is wrong. If this vision is wrong, why did the name 'darshan' even originate? Isn't darshan the dynamic course of action that distinguishes between what is and what is not! Who says it does not exist? What will happen if one speaks all sorts of nonsense, talks of literal knowledge, makes corrections using vowels and consonants, and merely performs intellectual gymnastics within the theory of Yoga? You will feel bad when I say this. It is a painful matter. I am speaking from my knowledge. Hindus have a limitation, Islam has a limitation, and similarly, all these mentioned visions have a limitation. It is when you go there that you see the predicament. No one will understand this even if they hear or see it. This is my experience. A system called fulfillment existed here. The word was received. Certain things must be done. They were done. It is not the Vedantic vision spoken of in logic. Is there any need to conduct mimamsa (critical investigation) here that eliminates dharma by bringing Vedanta into mere alphabetical knowledge? The result of that inner vision is, 'What is this, father, that you have shown me?' If these knowledgeable religious theorists fail to understand this, what can we do? Time is simply being wasted. It is about what needs to be done to prevent that from happening. That is the topic I must tell you along with the beginning of the Kali Yuga. Whether anyone asks or not, I will say this. The reason is that we lack the karma of imparting and absorbing love in the act of communicating face-to-face. Who are we telling this to? Who is being made to hear this? What is being said here? Aren't all these theorists speaking as if they came to praise and glorify a mistake? Do not adopt that theoretical approach. That is all I have to say to the people of this world. I have nothing else to say. Who am I to tell? I am merely conveying to you the sorrow that I have experienced.
Disciple: We have only one religion. The religion of love. We cannot attain salvation through any other religion.

Guru: It will never be possible. I have nothing to say to those who think it is possible. We have insulted the Gurus who showed us what that love is. Isn't this the truth? Now, if anyone has anything to say, let them say it. This is my experience that I am sharing. Then, God assigned a specific time period to each one. That is what we know now. Two thousand for one, five thousand for another, ten thousand for yet another—we do not receive any knowledge beyond what is said in this manner.
Guruvani
October 2006

It is the Yuga Dharma (the duty of the age) that we must understand. There is no point in presenting something without observing what must be observed in that particular era. Is this not our tradition? Have we not been born? Where will you go to correct yourselves now? We only have a very short lifespan. When looking at the grand vision of time, we do not exist even as a mere atom. What will we do here? This is where the truth lies. The knowledge of this doctrine, which pervades both the atomic and the infinite, must begin from the point it has reached. Otherwise, things will not be right. There is nothing to be gained by simply wandering here and there. That is just teaching people foolishness. It is not honesty. We have pushed out onto the veranda the standard of love established by our ancestors. This is the question the Prophet asked. They do not know this. None of us knows it either. All the Mahatmas who have come before and after have strayed from this Yuga Dharma and blocked the path. I do not know if one can study this deeply and say that fish and meat can be consumed together. You are all educated people. I am uneducated. Each of us is left out of the corridor of this sectarian trend, which makes us very sad. What will happen if we do not all feel that this is regrettable? If understanding that is our goal, love must be at the forefront. The respect for that love is required. You also need the wisdom to receive it with humility. Otherwise, it will not be Dharma; it will become Adharma. I respected that experience because, at one time, Mahatmas with all visions spoke of the greatness of scholars in that manner. However, scholars have also come. I am not saying they haven't. Within these five thousand years, many known Mahatmas have come. But the demonic vision they speak of is the remnant of the wicked deeds standing in their practical realm. Do not feel bad when I say this. It is a mistake that can happen to them. It is indeed a wicked deed. We understand this when these Mahatmas come one by one; I will not stand by my knowledge or acquaintance. This is where this calculation is told. We must see all these mentioned Mahatmas without exception. We must grasp that aspect of where they went wrong in their practical realm. Regardless, we cannot reject them and put something else in their place. How it is, we can speak in terms of the countless crores of people who believed and obeyed them, but a crore is not a magnitude here. If we do not accept their decadence, there is no other way. We cannot say it. We can say it, but we should not. You can only proceed by rejecting them. When we accept them, we are taking on that part. We have to experience it. That is one reason you asked. The youths who have come to me so far do not understand it at all.

Among them, only this Pai spoke a truth. Dr. Pai. How many years ago? Eight years ago. This is not a disease worth mentioning. Then I will give you medicine. If I do not experience this, there is another flaw. You will not be able to move forward. You can discard it as unwanted. Shouldn't we see it in the practical action combined with blood, flesh, and marrow? It is not there. I haven't told any of this to anyone here until now. So, seeing what happened to that Mahatma, we should not intellectualize that action but explain it. Are we to intellectualize it and hand it over to the scientists? When I say this, it becomes too much. They cannot do it. The illustrative experience for that is the very science you speak of. Where science hits a dead end, there stands God. If I tell them all this now, won't they mock me? Since you have no way to proceed, I said this to clear a path. The most difficult thing in this world is the action that our ancestors worshipped and made others worship. There is also no knowledge to sustain it. So, it is for this reason that the words spoken are indicated. Seeing this in detail is why it was asked, 'What are you doing to me, man?'
Disciple: The Prophet had to lament like that in the end.

Guru: That is what we must take into account. It is exactly this. The question asked, 'Father, have you forsaken me?' Why did you throw me among these demons? That is the sorrow. If there is no solution to this sorrow, there will be no solution to anything. When I say this, some will like it. If they like it, let them. Anyway, things won't work out just because you like it. Because my lifetime is just a fraction of an atom, isn't it? If I discard even this atom and leave, where will I go? We cannot take anything with us without this. The ultimate truth of a human being is love. If that love is without respect, it is not love. This is where it was lost. We need a person to figure out the path of that love. That is what was said. That is, as far as we are concerned, we should be able to carry this forward. But we can show it to them. Everyone in every religion has said that it will happen. None of them said it merely for the literal meaning of the words. Then what is so special about saying they have said it? It was said after completely gathering all this. This is the benefit of working in this intellectual realm. What will we do here? Once you understand this, there is no need to worry about us at all. That is the only proof I can give you.
Guruvani
November 2006

The author of the Gita has spoken of that special intellect to ponder how many eras have passed. We must respect that. All this running was done ultimately to fulfill that. Understood? Now, the path Jesus ran and the Prophet ran—didn't all these mentioned Mahatmas run? They ran to fulfill it. But they could not. Didn't we make it run from here? Where did it stop? Didn't it go and stop in another continent? Having gone there, wasn't this Dwaraka finished? Look at that Dwaraka even today, isn't it in the calculations? It is. That is one thing told to Arjuna. You take these children and women and save them. There is no other way now. So Sri Krishna, having told Arjuna what to do for this and having shown him, took him along. That is why the disciple was taken along; he was taken to repeatedly fulfill that disciple. What happened when they went there? It was an era where we could not identify the boundary of this action bridging the Yugas. So, Kali Yuga is this many years, Treta Yuga is this many years, Dvapara is this many years, and these three combined is Satya Yuga. Isn't this how we have been convinced? But what can be said about what lies in between this? Shouldn't it cross from one to another? How much time did that take? Is there such a condition? What should we do in this condition?
Disciple: When that change happens, it will become a beneficial change.
Guru: Yes. Is it enough if we just imagine it to be beneficial?
Disciple: We must naturally accept it. Water will turn into steam in that temporary state at a hundred degrees.
Guru: Yes. After becoming steam, won't it become water again? What is the recourse for that?
Disciple: That is the transformation of energy.
Guru: I do not know about energy or anything else. Will this become water or not?
Disciple: It will become water.

Guru: Where will it go? It will return. So that is it. That is exactly what was said. You give some parallel. I find nothing special in it. Is there such a thing or not? How can what exists be destroyed? Where will one go to destroy it?
Disciple: What exists can neither be destroyed nor created.
Guru: If we start speaking transcendently about such a state, where will we stand?
Disciple: We will get nowhere.

Guru: When every religious doctrine, karma doctrine, and yoga doctrine were combined, the exact condition changed. What has been divided into four epochs has manifested as this Yoga, Karma, Jnana, and Bhakti. According to the capacity of the jiva (soul), one can ascend through them. However, without recognizing the level at which the jiva's capacity stands, one simply practiced yoga, performed karma, or practiced bhakti and departed. It is not his fault. That is what he is within the society. Isn't it? How would he know? By what means would he know? Thus, it was first declared, "Vāsanamayam jagat sarvam" (The entire universe is infused with latent tendencies). Not just our entirety, did you understand? It means not entrusting total liberation to just one entity. Assigning knowledge, fortune, and significance to different epochs was a mistake. Herein lies the Yugantara Dharma (the duty across epochs). Who is to state this, who is to see it, and who is to undertake it?
Disciple: Isn't practicing the dharma of the respective epoch (yuga) the only thing that can be done?

Guru: That is true, but about this epoch — one person says five thousand. Another says two lakhs, yet another claims it is even more. Another person asserts it is over four lakhs. Then another states it as eight thousand or nine thousand. It goes on like that, mentioning figures beyond four lakhs, nine lakhs, and sixteen lakhs. What can be done about this? Do we face such an entanglement before us?
Disciple: Yes.
Guru: The question is how to untie it. Do you agree that demons exist?
Disciple: Yes.
Guru: Then is there a God (Deva)? Is there a prophet?
Disciple: Yes.
Guru: Is there not a designated period for the Guru?
Disciple: Yes.
Guru: Then isn't there a Kala Dharma (duty of the times)?
Disciple: Yes.
Guru: What should be done here?
Disciple: In each Kala Dharma, does not that jiva function in accordance with its individual nature?
Guru: It can only function in that manner. Thus, we stand beneath the visionary who emerged through the beliefs or customs shaped by the jiva's past actions.
Disciple: Is not one continuously born into the very state that one has attained?
Guru: When you say being born... Didn't we say earlier that it will turn into water again?
Disciple: If it becomes water, isn't it becoming water while waiting for completeness?
Guru: Yes. What doubt is there about that?
Disciple: If a sprouted seed is roasted, it will not sprout again, will it?

Guru: Having said that this copra (dried coconut) will not sprout, it would be good if there were no other copras. I am speaking about their yogic calculations. If there are no other coconuts, your copra will not sprout. For it to become a copra like that, whatever times and periods need to be lost must indeed be lost. Shouldn't they? Isn't it the evolutionary state of the jiva? Wasn't it said that it should cease to exist? We have not seen to what extent that goes. One should speak only if one has seen it. Then, which skies does this evolutionary state belong to? That is this Nalukettu (traditional four-part structure). There are also those who say, 'He who hasn't built ten is a pig'. Let him build it. When practicing all these yoga methods, I am speaking in your language. So there is this Nalukettu. Shouldn't we know what it was tied with and what broke it? So this is how we must understand it. The reason is that specific doctrines were brought and bound upon us without knowing the duration of the yuga dharmas. We have not received the correction regarding what the dharma is to retrieve what has come and gone. We must understand it. So, if we cross the four skies, we must articulate what the dharma is that crosses the seven realms (Bhumikas) that are mentioned. Would yogis disbelieve that? I am saying that it will go and stand up to there.
Guruvani
December 2006

There is a custom of hanging down south. You haven't heard of it, right? When a king was traveling along the way, a woman was standing there displaying excellent singing, dancing, and performance. Thinking she possessed artistic talent, he called her, took her with him, and taught her everything necessary. He even married her himself. He married her, and eventually, he set out to tour the country. He went out several times. During one of these trips, when they reached a certain place, she asked, "Does that hang without being tied, or is it tied and hanging?" Which one is it? She asked this when they arrived beneath a tree called 'Aatuvanchi', where she used to play. It produces a stem about a foot long. You know the mango stalk? Like that, a very long stalk emerges. It is called Aatuvanchi. At the end of it, there will be a fruit. It was while she was playing beneath it that the king had taken her away. When she came riding an elephant to see the country, she asked the king whether it was tied up or if it naturally grew that way. "Is it tied and hanging or hanging without being tied?" He dropped her off there and departed, telling her to return only after learning whether it hangs tied or untied. Instructing her to observe it properly, he left her there and went away. Isn't our story similar to this?

There is such a profound error residing within us. We must see who is the inheritor of this Yuga Dharma. That is why it was said — we need not pursue any of the others. How many acharyas will it take to resolve this — observe this. The dharma of a yuga, then the dharma of a chatur-yuga, and thus how many dharmas of chatur-yugas — a Manvantara. The reason is that this matter was not clearly stated. Simply tallying numbers and altering letters will not work. It must be resolved right there. Then what is this Yuga Dharma? The author of the Gita has stated, 'Kali is in the Shudra'. Then who is this Shudra? Anyone who is not a Brahma-jnani (knower of Brahman) is indeed a Shudra. So it means this Shudra must become a Brahma-jnani. Isn't it? That is precisely why Krishna was brought and placed in your lap. You did not accept him. You trampled and suppressed him. Therefore, this could not be fulfilled. These devas and deceivers standing together — who are these deceivers? That is, Sri Krishna, having labored so hard and waited for ages for us, is demonstrating all his accomplishments to Arjuna. He bestowed upon Arjuna the mastery of weapons. After that, what is witnessed upon reaching there? "Look at this, Arjuna; instead of ruining things by practicing yoga as preached, look at this," Sri Krishna is saying. He looked and saw, right? He saw, accepted it, and took everyone along. Then the running commenced with them once again. Right? Running to attain the longevity of ages. What is meant by the longevity of ages is, suppose we discovered a time-span of fifty thousand years or a crore years; can we live that long and then depart? Then aren't we living without truly having lived? That is the truth. Until that truth is perceived, is it acceptable to simply proclaim this as the truth? A far-sight (vision) of these fifty thousand years and a lakh years was established: agreed. But can we proceed by claiming there is no such far-sight?
Disciple: No.

Guru: Then shouldn't the remainder of what exists be seen? Even today, the Christians do not perceive that era. Do we not harbor the ignorance that teaches that by reasserting him as 'beyond time', he washed away the sins? That is, they declared this and committed murder. Having killed, all those who orchestrated the killing died. After they passed away, it is being preached, using his very religion, that the Lord washed away all these sins. What kind of teaching is this? Then they bear no sin, do they? Aren't we all perfectly pure? Thus, there is a profound ignorance in teaching religious doctrines in this manner.
Disciple: It exists in all religions.

Guru: Yes. So, after saying this, the people who have started saying Pentecost at the end, what is it - they say Hallelujah, Hallelujah. They are speaking that language. So, the question was whether it is correct to say that they are speaking in tongues. This was not said to insult anyone. Isn't this our situation? As long as we do not understand that it is not like that, we will keep saying the same thing. So, we cannot just talk about these four heavens and seven heavens, and talk only about this solar system and move on. Understood? There are so many solar systems. When we say galaxies, aren't they clusters? Where will the calculation of stars, which is being tallied here based on the calculation of a total of twenty-seven stars, lead to? So, the change of one solar system itself is the change of many solar systems. The issue is that this is not understood this way. We see this revolving like a earth, sun, and moon. But this revolving goes from days to years to ages - no need to go to ages. Don't we say a Jupiter cycle? This Jupiter revolves and comes back in twelve years. Isn't our age being acquired? Do you want to know where we have reached in its acquired karma? This is not to say it doesn't exist. It certainly exists. If everything exists, we should go there and correct even the philosophy. Otherwise, there is no justification for this. It's not about taking a bath after preaching Vedanta. We are empty in the aspect of knowledge. Then, one should not say that what exists does not exist. If you say 'emptiness', you shouldn't say that. That is why it is said 'everything exists, the peak of philosophy'. If it exists like this, where does it stand? Shouldn't we start from where it stands? Without seeing where it stands, from where will we start? This is how we are. So, we haven't even been told how long a solar system, where this dharma of ages and Jupiter cycles has increased, will last. So many ages have been counted; this solar system - shouldn't it burn out? What is said is that the calculation of this burning out over time has not been told. This is where we stand. Everyone became like this. You should not move forward saying that what these great people said does not exist, nor should you go saying that there is only sorrow in your life. There is sorrow in everyone's life. If you abandon the dharma that can take this sorrow as happiness and say that the path of karma based on your whimsical imaginations is right, you will be ruined. This is what you don't understand. Do we need this or not? My father, my father's father - we will see what condition controlled them. If you say this doesn't exist and say it is where mother is, where father is, it won't work; father should be where mother is, and mother should be where father is. Wherever those life-givers stand, that must be broken out. This is 'karma became bindings for man'. Then who is man? The soul. 'Only when bindings are cut will liberation come for sure'. 'Liberation' is spoken of in different times. So, this Guru and the disciple of the Guru must be the inheritors of the dharma that satisfies these times. At least during our lifetime, we should be able to understand what this means. After that, children, I can live seeing you. Who should say it? A father should say it to his children. Then what should the mother say? You should see the karma of the father's clear mind corresponding to the calculation of the sky.
